studies.citation: Burthe, S.J., et al. (2016) Do early warning indicators consistently predict nonlinear change in long-term ecological data? Journal of Applied Ecology 53:666-676
studies.data_system: 126 long-term abundance data sets from 55 taxa across multiple trophic levels in marine and freshwater ecosystems (specific databases not visible in search results)
studies.outcome_definition: significant nonlinear change in abundance time series (as visible in snippet); collapse threshold not visible in search results
studies.key_finding: Time series containing true positives were uncommon (8% for variance; 6% for autocorrelation); all but one time series also contained false classifications; 43% of time series were categorized differently by variance versus autocorrelation; authors conclude variance and autocorrelation in abundance data consistently fail to predict nonlinear change and recommend multivariate/driver-informed approaches.
studies.notes: Closest existing multi-series TP/FP accounting for abundance EWS; appears to be a whole-series classification (EWS trend vs. presence of nonlinear change) rather than sequential fixed-horizon forecasting. Full co-author list not visible in search results.

studies.citation: Litzow, M.A., Mueter, F.J., Urban, J.D. (2013) Rising catch variability preceded historical fisheries collapses in Alaska. Ecological Applications
studies.data_system: Spatially resolved catch data from 14 Gulf of Alaska/Bering Sea crustacean fisheries (12 collapsing, 2 non-collapsing), 278 cumulative years; sampling unit = ADF&G statistical reporting area (mean 42 areas per fishery, range 7-81)
studies.outcome_definition: fishery collapse (exact threshold not visible in search results)
studies.baseline_comparator: two non-collapsing fisheries served as contrasts; no state/trend forecasting baseline visible
studies.key_finding: A random-effects model across 12 collapsing fisheries showed strong evidence of increasing spatial catch variability 1-4 years prior to collapse; individual trends were statistically significant for only 4 of 12 collapsing fisheries; trends in variability differed significantly between collapsing and non-collapsing fisheries, suggesting rising variability is most useful when pooled across multiple populations.
studies.notes: Lead time reported (1-4 years). Only 2 negative controls, so false-alarm rate is weakly constrained. Spatial (not temporal) variance.

studies.citation: Gsell, A.S., et al. (2016) Evaluating early-warning indicators of critical transitions in natural aquatic ecosystems. PNAS
studies.data_system: Long-term monitoring datasets of five freshwater ecosystems (lakes) that experienced sudden, persistent transitions
studies.outcome_definition: sudden, persistent transitions in lake state (details not visible in search results)
studies.key_finding: Four commonly used early-warning indicators assessed on five well-monitored lakes; at present EWIs do not provide reliable and consistent signals of impending critical transitions.
studies.notes: Full author list, indicator names and quantitative detection rates not visible in search results. Relevant to the planned lake challenge analysis.

studies.citation: O'Brien, D.A., et al. (2023) Early warning signals have limited applicability to empirical lake data. Nature Communications
studies.data_system: Empirical lake time series (monthly and yearly resolutions); specific lakes/databases not visible in search results
studies.outcome_definition: lake transitions; 'true positive' and 'true negative' time series categories referenced in snippet
studies.baseline_comparator: chance (0.5 probability) as implicit reference; a recent machine-learning EWS model also evaluated
studies.key_finding: Most indicators did not perform better than chance; multivariate EWSs were weakly superior to univariate; a recent machine-learning model performed poorly. A snippet (attribution to this paper inferred from the eigenMAF indicator, medium confidence) states no indicator displayed reliability across resolutions or true-positive/true-negative time series better than 0.5 probability, with eigenMAF highest (monthly true = 0.62; yearly true = 0.70).
studies.notes: Detailed AUC tables not visible in search results. The 0.62/0.70 figures came from a search summary that did not explicitly name the paper; treat as medium confidence.

studies.citation: Zhang, F., et al. (2020) Early warning signals of population productivity regime shifts in global fisheries. Ecological Indicators
studies.data_system: 191 global fisheries populations (database not visible in search results; likely stock-assessment derived)
studies.outcome_definition: observed productivity regime shifts (definition method not visible in search results)
studies.key_finding: Evaluated SD and AR1 in predicting observed productivity regime shifts of 191 global fisheries populations; successful EWS provided more than five years warning for more than 50% of populations; SD and AR1 were simultaneously detected in less than 50% of population regime shifts, suggesting critical transitions may not be the major cause of observed regime shifts.
studies.notes: Lead author 'F. Zhang' is the only author visible; DOI not visible in search results. Productivity shifts, not abundance collapse.

studies.citation: Cano, Jensen & Dakos (2025) Identifying fish populations prone to abrupt shifts via dynamical footprint analysis. PNAS 122(34):e2505461122
studies.data_system: Fish population biomass time series from three global datasets (dataset names not visible in search results); 11 Large Marine Ecosystem regions
studies.outcome_definition: time series classified into abrupt vs. nonabrupt shape classes
studies.key_finding: Mechanism-agnostic machine-learning approach classifies biomass time series as abrupt/nonabrupt and predicts class from dynamical-footprint metrics (variance, autocorrelation, etc.); populations prone to abrupt shifts detected with moderate accuracy despite data limitations; 50 populations identified as at risk of future abrupt shifts.
studies.notes: Closest recent fisheries-wide ML study using EWS-type features with non-abrupt series included, but appears to be whole-series classification rather than sequential fixed-horizon forecasting. Accuracy numbers not visible in search results.

studies.citation: [authors not visible in search results] (2026) Abrupt declines in fish productivity often precede stock collapses in marine fisheries. [journal not visible; PMC13537261]
studies.data_system: 315 marine fish stocks (database not visible in search results)
studies.outcome_definition: stock collapse (definition not visible); abrupt productivity shifts detected
studies.key_finding: Productivity abrupt shifts detected in more than a quarter of 315 stocks; abrupt productivity declines preceded stock collapses by ten to twenty years in 25% of the cases that shifted; declines overrepresented in fastest-warming regions.
studies.notes: Productivity-shift detection rather than classical CSD EWS; useful as a candidate covariate/alternative indicator. Journal, DOI and authors not visible.

studies.citation: Clements, C.F. & Ozgul, A. (2016) Including trait-based early warning signals helps predict population collapse. Nature Communications
studies.data_system: Microcosm experiment (species not visible in search results) with abundance and body-size time series
studies.outcome_definition: experimentally induced population collapse
studies.key_finding: Including fitness-related trait (body size) dynamics in composite EWS gave significantly more reliable early warnings than abundance-only metrics; a follow-up preprint reports alternate weightings improve composite EWS by decreasing false-positive and increasing true-positive frequencies.
studies.notes: Quantitative TP/FP rates not visible in search results.

studies.citation: Clements, Blanchard, Nash, Hindell & Ozgul (2017) Body size shifts and early warning signals precede the historic collapse of whale stocks. Nature Ecology & Evolution 1(7):188
studies.data_system: Commercial whaling catch and body-size records over ~70 years
studies.outcome_definition: global collapse of whale stocks (exact criterion not visible)
studies.baseline_comparator: abundance-only EWS vs. combined abundance+body-size EWS
studies.key_finding: Mean body size of caught whales declined by up to 4 m over 70 years; EWS detectable up to 40 years before global collapse; combining abundance and body-size data reduced the time-series length required and decreased the chance of false-positive predictions.
studies.notes: Retrospective single-system case; a later comment questioned reliability of whaling catch data for body-size analyses (reply published).

studies.citation: Cerini, F., Childs, D.Z., Clements, C.F. (2023) A predictive timeline of wildlife population collapse. Nature Ecology & Evolution 7(3):320-331
studies.data_system: Conceptual framework (no new empirical dataset visible)
studies.outcome_definition: population collapse under external stressors
studies.key_finding: Proposes a predictable sequence of individual-level (behaviour, morphology) changes preceding abundance-based EWS and collapse; argues predictive ecology should shift away from abundance-only data.
studies.notes: Framework paper; relevant for framing why abundance-only EWS may underperform.

studies.citation: Cerini, F., et al. (2025) Multivariate signals of population collapse in a high-throughput ecological experiment. Ecology 106(9):e70197
studies.data_system: Autonomously monitored high-throughput Paramecium caudatum microcosms forced to collapse by gradual pollutant introduction
studies.outcome_definition: abundance decline/collapse under pollutant stress
studies.key_finding: Predictable sequence: declines in movement speed, then body length, then emergence of abundance-based EWS, then abundance declines; phenotypic signals detectable up to 1.65 generations before significant abundance decrease and a whole generation before a detectable EWS (per snippet on related work).
studies.notes: True/false positive metrics not visible in search results. Data/code on Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.14833814).

studies.citation: Arkilanian, A.A., Clements, C.F., Ozgul, A., Baruah, G. (2020) Effect of time series length and resolution on abundance- and trait-based early warning signals of population declines. Ecology 101:e03040
studies.data_system: Model simulations plus Didinium nasutum microcosm populations
studies.outcome_definition: population collapse in microcosm/simulation
studies.key_finding: Simulations suggest a minimum of 5-10 generations of data for accurate abundance-based EWS; including trait information halves the required length; no evident decrease in EWS performance as resolution decreased.
studies.notes: Directly informs minimum series length criteria for the preregistration.

studies.citation: Burant, J.B., et al. (2021) Early warning indicators of population collapse in a seasonal environment. Journal of Animal Ecology
studies.data_system: not visible in search results (experimental populations in a seasonal environment)
studies.outcome_definition: population collapse
studies.key_finding: Surfaced repeatedly alongside false-positive/lead-time queries; substantive results not visible in search results.
studies.notes: Needs full-text check.

studies.citation: Drake, J.M. & Griffen, B.D. (2010) Early warning signals of extinction in deteriorating environments. Nature 467:456-459
studies.data_system: Experimental Daphnia magna populations under deteriorating environment, with healthy control populations
studies.outcome_definition: extinction/tipping point in experimental populations
studies.key_finding: Critical slowing down indicators anticipated extinction in stressed Daphnia populations relative to control populations.
studies.notes: Foundational experimental demonstration; no ROC/lead-time accounting visible.

studies.citation: Dai, L., Vorselen, D., Korolev, K.S., Gore, J. (2012) Generic indicators for loss of resilience before a tipping point leading to population collapse. Science 336(6085):1175-1177
studies.data_system: Replicate laboratory yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) populations with experimentally mapped bifurcation diagram
studies.outcome_definition: population collapse at experimentally mapped tipping point
studies.key_finding: Fluctuations in population density increased in size and duration near the tipping point, consistent with critical slowing down.
studies.notes: Experimental validation; not a forecast-skill study.

studies.citation: Clements, C.F., Drake, J.M., Griffiths, J.I., Ozgul, A. (2015) Factors influencing the detectability of early warning signals of population collapse. American Naturalist 186(1):50-58
studies.data_system: not visible in search results
studies.outcome_definition: population collapse
studies.key_finding: Widely cited on factors affecting EWS detectability; specific results not visible in search results.
studies.notes: Needs full-text check.

studies.citation: Jarvis-Cross, M., Kirk, D., Krichel, L., Luijckx, P., Molnár, P.K., Krkošek, M. (2025) Early warning signals do not predict a warming-induced experimental epidemic. PLOS Global Public Health
studies.data_system: Experimental Daphnia magna-Ordospora colligata disease system (warming vs. control populations) plus simulations
studies.outcome_definition: climate-mediated epidemic emergence (critical transition to epidemic state)
studies.baseline_comparator: control populations held at sub-epidemic temperature
studies.key_finding: EWS of epidemic emergence were nearly as likely to be detected in control populations as in warming populations, implying ubiquitous false positives may limit EWS reliability.
studies.notes: Ecological host-parasite population experiment with explicit negative controls; strong evidence for the false-alarm-budget rationale.

studies.citation: Jarvis, L., et al. (2016) Early warning signals detect critical impacts of experimental warming. Ecology and Evolution
studies.data_system: Model parameterized by experimental growth rates; experimental populations (species not visible)
studies.outcome_definition: thermally induced extinction/critical threshold
studies.key_finding: Model parameterized by experimental growth rates exhibits critical slowing down near an experimentally tested threshold; simulated data suggest EWS can anticipate a thermal tipping point; more data across temperatures needed to evaluate CSD in experimental populations.
studies.notes: Full author list not visible (only 'Jarvis' visible).

studies.citation: Bury, T.M., et al. (2021) Deep learning for early warning signals of tipping points. PNAS 118(39):e2106140118
studies.data_system: Simulated bifurcation models (May harvesting fold, consumer-resource Hopf/transcritical, behaviour-disease) plus empirical: Mediterranean sediment anoxia transitions, thermoacoustic Hopf bifurcation experiments, paleoclimate ice-core transitions
studies.outcome_definition: approach to bifurcation (forced vs. null/non-bifurcating series)
studies.baseline_comparator: variance and lag-1 autocorrelation (Kendall tau) as comparator EWS; ROC/AUC
studies.key_finding: Deep-learning classifier trained on generic simulated bifurcations evaluated via ROC curves and AUC against variance and lag-1 autocorrelation for predicting upcoming transitions, including on empirical geochemical and thermoacoustic data.
studies.notes: Numerical AUCs not visible in search results. Few ecological population series; serves as the capacity-matched-learner precedent.

studies.citation: Bury, T.M., et al. (2023) Predicting discrete-time bifurcations with deep learning. [journal not visible; PMC10564974]
studies.data_system: Simulations from physiology, economics and ecology models plus experimental chick-heart aggregate data
studies.outcome_definition: discrete-time bifurcations
studies.key_finding: Classifier for discrete-time bifurcations showed higher sensitivity and specificity than commonly used EWS across a wide range of noise intensities.
studies.notes: Not population-abundance data.

studies.citation: Deb, S., Sidheekh, S., Clements, C.F., Krishnan, N.C., Dutta, P.S. (2022) Machine learning methods trained on simple models can predict critical transitions in complex natural systems. Royal Society Open Science 9(2):211475
studies.data_system: Simulated training data; empirical test systems 'ranging from rapid climatic change to the collapse of ecological populations' (specific datasets not visible)
studies.outcome_definition: catastrophic vs non-catastrophic critical transitions
studies.key_finding: EWSNet deep network trained on simple theoretical models reliably predicted observed real-world transitions including ecological population collapses and distinguished catastrophic from non-catastrophic transitions.
studies.notes: The O'Brien et al. 2023 lake paper reports a recent ML EWS model performing poorly on lake data (which model not visible).

studies.citation: Grziwotz, F., et al. (2023) Anticipating the occurrence and type of critical transitions. Science Advances
studies.data_system: Three empirical cases: cyanobacteria microcosm, voice onset, end of last greenhouse earth
studies.outcome_definition: approach to bifurcation (|DEV| approaching 1)
studies.key_finding: Dynamical eigenvalue (DEV) from empirical dynamic modeling approaches 1 near bifurcation and its complex-plane position indicates transition type; demonstrated on three empirical systems.
studies.notes: A 2024 Theoretical Ecology follow-up ('Efficacy of dynamic eigenvalue...') exists (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12080-024-00593-5); details not visible.

studies.citation: Rohde, E., Pearce, N.J.T., Young, J., Xenopoulos, M.A. (2022) Applying early warning indicators to predict critical transitions in a lake undergoing multiple changes. Ecological Applications 32(7):e2685
studies.data_system: Lake Simcoe, Ontario long-term and high-frequency sensor data
studies.outcome_definition: breakpoints in state variables
studies.key_finding: Retrospective evaluation of agreement between SD, autocorrelation, skewness, kurtosis and breakpoints in a recovering eutrophic lake; suggests high-frequency sensors have potential for real-time EWIs.
studies.notes: Single-lake retrospective; no forecast-skill metrics visible.

studies.citation: Carpenter, S.R., et al. (2011) Early Warnings of Regime Shifts: A Whole-Ecosystem Experiment. Science
studies.data_system: Whole-lake manipulation (top predator addition over 3 years) with adjacent reference lake
studies.outcome_definition: food-web regime shift
studies.key_finding: Warning signals were evident in the manipulated lake more than a year before the food-web transition was complete; reference lake monitored simultaneously.
studies.notes: Full author list only partly visible ('Carpenter et al.'). Single manipulated/reference pair.

studies.citation: Litzow, M.A. & Hunsicker, M.E. (2016) Early warning signals, nonlinearity, and signs of hysteresis in real ecosystems. Ecosphere 7:e01614
studies.data_system: Review/meta-analysis of published EWS studies plus eight northeast Pacific Ocean time series
studies.outcome_definition: ecological transitions in published studies; nonlinearity tests
studies.baseline_comparator: alternative explanations: red noise, linear tracking, transients
studies.key_finding: Published studies demonstrating nonlinear dynamics were more likely to support EWS predictions; NE Pacific series often too short for formal nonlinearity tests; many published EWS examples may be more parsimoniously explained by autocorrelated random variability, linear reversible tracking, or transients.
studies.notes: Supports the need for null/baseline comparators.

studies.citation: Perretti, C.T. & Munch, S.B. (2012) Regime shift indicators fail under noise levels commonly observed in ecological systems. Ecological Applications 22(6):1772-1779
studies.data_system: Simulated three-species model with field-like noise
studies.outcome_definition: simulated regime shift
studies.key_finding: Early-warning indicators performed poorly when simulated data had noise levels similar to real ecological data.
studies.notes: Simulation only; DOI not visible in search results.

studies.citation: Jäger, G. & Füllsack, M. (2019) Systematically false positives in early warning signal analysis. PLOS ONE
studies.data_system: Simulated systems (classes of systems that always show EWS without critical transitions)
studies.outcome_definition: presence/absence of critical transition in simulated systems
studies.key_finding: Systematic false positives are common; whole classes of systems always show EWS without critical transitions; rolling-window linear detrending removed false positives whereas scaling methods did not.
studies.notes: Methodological; supports preprocessing choices in the preregistration.

studies.citation: Boettiger, C. & Hastings, A. (2012) Quantifying limits to detection of early warning for critical transitions. Journal of the Royal Society Interface
studies.data_system: Simulated systems; empirical Daphnia experimental data referenced as example
studies.outcome_definition: approach to critical transition vs stable system
studies.baseline_comparator: stable (null) system distribution of test statistic
studies.key_finding: Introduces ROC-based comparison of summary statistics (e.g., Kendall's tau) with false-positive rate computed from the null/stable-system distribution at each threshold, quantifying false alarms vs failed detections.
studies.notes: Companion paper 'Early warning signals and the prosecutor's fallacy' (arXiv 1210.1204) discusses base-rate issues. Author list inferred from arXiv/PMC listing; DOI not visible.

studies.citation: Dakos, V., et al. (2012) Methods for detecting early warnings of critical transitions in time series illustrated using simulated ecological data. PLOS ONE
studies.data_system: Simulated ecological data
studies.outcome_definition: simulated critical transitions
studies.key_finding: Reference methods paper for rolling-window AR1/variance/Kendall tau EWS computation (basis of the earlywarnings toolbox).
studies.notes: Author list beyond Dakos not visible in search results.

studies.citation: Dakos, V., Glaser, S.M., Hsieh, C.-H., Sugihara, G. (2017) Elevated nonlinearity as an indicator of shifts in the dynamics of populations under stress. Journal of the Royal Society Interface
studies.data_system: Ricker-type simulation of a fisheries population transitioning to boom-bust or overexploitation
studies.outcome_definition: transition to overexploitation / irregular dynamics
studies.key_finding: Variance and nonlinearity increase similarly along both transitions; elevated nonlinearity proposed as an indicator of dynamic shifts under stress.
studies.notes: Simulation; DOI not visible.

studies.citation: Krkošek, M. & Drake, J.M. (2014) On signals of phase transitions in salmon population dynamics. Proceedings of the Royal Society B 281:20133221
studies.data_system: not visible in search results (salmon population dynamics)
studies.outcome_definition: phase transitions in salmon dynamics
studies.key_finding: Existence confirmed; substantive results not visible in search results.
studies.notes: Needs full-text check; DOI not visible.

studies.citation: Brett, T.S. & Rohani, P. (2020) Dynamical footprints enable detection of disease emergence. PLOS Biology
studies.data_system: Simulated training data; empirical incidence: mumps England (mid-2000s), pertussis US post-1980, dengue Puerto Rico, plague Madagascar 2017
studies.outcome_definition: disease (re-)emergence
studies.key_finding: Supervised classifier trained on simulated CSD footprints anticipated mumps reemergence 4 years in advance and identified resurgent pertussis states with increasing accuracy from 1980, reliable classification from 1992.
studies.notes: Epidemiological, not ecological populations; precedent for simulation-trained classifiers applied sequentially to empirical data.

studies.citation: O'Brien, D.A. & Clements, C.F. (2021) Early warning signal reliability varies with COVID-19 waves. Biology Letters
studies.data_system: Daily COVID-19 case data across 24 countries
studies.outcome_definition: nonlinear (exponential) case increases / waves
studies.key_finding: Sequential composite EWS (variance, autocorrelation, skewness) could predict nonlinear case increases but reliability varied by wave; UK: wave 1 undetected, wave 2 pre-empted by 48 days, wave 3 lagged by 10 days; accuracy highest when R was suppressed for a long period before the outbreak.
studies.notes: Explicit 'novel sequential analysis' (rolling/expanding origins) - a design precedent from the same group that built EWSmethods.

studies.citation: Proverbio, D., Kemp, F., Magni, S., Gonçalves, J. (2022) Performance of early warning signals for disease re-emergence: A case study on COVID-19 data. PLOS Computational Biology 18(3):e1009958
studies.data_system: COVID-19 case data, several countries, subsequent waves
studies.outcome_definition: emergence of subsequent epidemic waves
studies.key_finding: Variance and autocorrelation EWS could be useful against new outbreaks but may fail to detect rapid or noisy shifts in epidemic dynamics.
studies.notes: Sensitivity/specificity/lead-time numbers not visible in search results.

studies.citation: Dablander, F., Heesterbeek, H., Borsboom, D., Drake, J.M. (2022) Overlapping timescales obscure early warning signals of the second COVID-19 wave. Proceedings of the Royal Society B 289(1968):20211809
studies.data_system: COVID-19 case data, European countries
studies.outcome_definition: second epidemic wave
studies.key_finding: Contrary to theory, CSD indicators generally decreased rather than increased before the second wave; explained by transient multi-timescale relaxation; CSD theory applies only when forcing is slow relative to internal dynamics.
studies.notes: Cautionary evidence on non-stationary forcing; code on GitHub.

studies.citation: Harris, M.J., et al. (2020) Early warning signals of malaria resurgence in Kericho, Kenya. Biology Letters
studies.data_system: Monthly Plasmodium falciparum case incidence, Kericho, Kenya (single site)
studies.outcome_definition: April 1993 malaria resurgence
studies.key_finding: 5 of 10 CSD indicators increased before resurgence; warning signals appeared as early as 65 months prior; first test on real vector-borne disease data.
studies.notes: Full author list not visible; single positive case, no negatives.

studies.citation: Gao, Chakraborty, Greiner, Lewis & Wang (2025) Early detection of disease outbreaks and non-outbreaks using incidence data: A framework using feature-based time series classification and machine learning. PLOS Computational Biology
studies.data_system: Synthetic and real-world incidence datasets (real datasets not named in search results)
studies.outcome_definition: future outbreak vs non-outbreak sequences
studies.key_finding: 22 statistical features plus 5 EWS indicators differ between outbreak and non-outbreak sequences long before outbreaks; classifier AUC ranged from 0.99 (large expanding training windows) to 0.7 (small rolling windows).
studies.notes: Explicit non-outbreak class and expanding/rolling window evaluation - close in spirit to the intended design, in epidemiology.

studies.citation: Southall, E., Brett, T.S., Tildesley, M.J., Dyson, L. (2021) Early warning signals of infectious disease transitions: a review. Journal of the Royal Society Interface 18(182):20210555
studies.data_system: Review (pertussis, mumps, dengue, plague applications discussed)
studies.outcome_definition: disease emergence/elimination transitions
studies.key_finding: Comprehensive review of EWS for disease emergence/elimination including the logistic composite measure and applications to pertussis, mumps, dengue and plague.
studies.notes: Useful for the epidemiology evaluation-design literature.

studies.citation: Ward, E.J., Holmes, E.E., Thorson, J.T., Collen, B. (2014) Complexity is costly: a meta-analysis of parametric and non-parametric methods for short-term population forecasting. Oikos 123(6):652-661
studies.data_system: Population time series from the Global Population Dynamics Database (plus fish time series per reproduction report)
studies.outcome_definition: short-term abundance forecast error (not collapse)
studies.key_finding: Low-dimensional parametric autoregressive models gave the most accurate short-term forecasts across taxa; the most accurate model simply treated the most recent observation as the forecast; complex parametric and non-parametric models did worse except for highly cyclic species.
studies.notes: Key precedent for the state/trend baseline: on GPDD, naive/last-value forecasts are hard to beat. DOI not visible in search results.

studies.citation: Holmes, E.E., Sabo, J.L., Viscido, S.V., Fagan, W.F. (2007) A statistical approach to quasi-extinction forecasting. Ecology Letters 10:1182-1198
studies.data_system: not visible in search results
studies.outcome_definition: quasi-extinction (threshold crossing) risk
studies.key_finding: Argues accurate quasi-extinction forecasting does not require mechanistic knowledge because stochastic multiplicative growth converges to common statistical forms across many population processes.
studies.notes: Theoretical basis for the local-linear state-space threshold-crossing baseline.

studies.citation: [authors not visible in search results] (2019) Early warning signals of recovery in complex systems. Nature Communications
studies.data_system: Trait-based ecological model plus real-world fisheries data (database not visible)
studies.outcome_definition: recovery of overexploited stocks
studies.baseline_comparator: abundance-only vs trait-only vs combined EWS
studies.key_finding: Both abundance- and trait-based signals were independently detectable prior to recovery of stocks; combining them gave the best predictions of recovery.
studies.notes: Recovery, not collapse; authors not visible in search results.

studies.citation: [authors not visible in search results] (2026) Early Warning Signals in Ecological Time-Series. Entropy 28(6):628
studies.data_system: Review (simulated forced vs null series for ROC)
studies.outcome_definition: approach to bifurcation
studies.key_finding: Recent review: Kendall tau values used as discrimination thresholds to build ROC curves against forced vs null series; notes that in fold-bifurcation systems relevant to depensatory recruitment in exploited fish stocks, classical EWS may invert into 'critical speeding up' (variance/AC decreasing), recommending two-sided trend tests.
studies.notes: Directional-sign caveat is directly relevant to the prespecified EWS score for fisheries.

studies.citation: [authors not visible in search results] (2025) Early warnings are too late when parameters change rapidly. Scientific Reports
studies.data_system: not visible in search results (likely simulation)
studies.outcome_definition: not visible
studies.key_finding: Title-level evidence that EWS lead time collapses under rapid parameter change; content not visible in search results.
studies.notes: Surfaced only as a title; needs full-text check.

notes: Search limitations: per instructions, only WebSearch was used (no WebFetch/curl attempts), so all design fields reflect what was visible in search-result snippets/summaries; many papers' quantitative TP/FP/AUC tables, author lists and DOIs were not visible and are marked accordingly. Several search summaries were LLM-synthesized; where a claim could not be tied unambiguously to a specific paper (e.g., the eigenMAF 0.62/0.70 figures attributed to O'Brien et al. 2023) I flagged medium confidence. No hits surfaced for EWS evaluations using the Living Planet Database, BioTIME, ICES/FishGlob survey indices, or GPDD specifically (queries 26-27 returned only microcosm/whale papers); the closest large-scale fisheries studies are Zhang et al. 2020 (191 populations, Ecol Indic), Cano/Jensen/Dakos 2025 (three global fish datasets, PNAS) and Litzow et al. 2013 (14 Alaska fisheries). Overall gap assessment relevant to the novelty claim: the studies found either (a) classify whole series post hoc (Burthe 2016, Cano 2025, O'Brien 2023), (b) are single-system retrospectives without negatives (Clements 2017, Harris 2020, Gsell 2016), or (c) implement sequential/rolling-origin evaluation only in epidemiology (O'Brien & Clements 2021; Brett & Rohani 2020; Gao et al. 2025). No study visibly combined sequential fixed-horizon origins + held-out validation + matched state/trend forecasting baselines + threshold calibration to a common false-alarm budget + explicit handling of right-censored origins for population-abundance collapse across realms. Ward et al. 2014 (GPDD) is the key precedent that naive last-observation/low-order AR forecasts are hard to beat, supporting the planned state/trend baseline. The 2026 Entropy review's note on 'critical speeding up' in depensatory fish stocks is a directional caveat for the prespecified AR1/variance trend score. Candidate additional checks not run here: Southall et al. 2020 PLoS Comput Biol discrete-event EWS; Weinans et al. multivariate indicator evaluations; Ditlevsen & Johnsen 2010 (climate) on wishful thinking/false positives.

studies.citation: Zhang F (2020) Early warning signals of population productivity regime shifts in global fisheries. Ecological Indicators 115:106371
studies.data_system: 191 global fisheries populations; snippet states data from the RAM Legacy Stock Assessment Database were examined
studies.outcome_definition: Observed productivity (surplus-production) regime shifts; operational definition not visible in search results
studies.baseline_comparator: None visible in search results (SD and AR1 evaluated as EWS; no state/trend comparator mentioned)
studies.key_finding: Evaluated two EWS (standard deviation and AR1 coefficient) for predicting observed productivity regime shifts in 191 global fisheries populations; 'successful' EWS gave more than 5 years warning for more than 50% of populations; the author also concluded that critical transitions may not be a major cause of regime shifts in global fisheries.
studies.notes: Closest prior work to a fisheries-wide EWS hindcast on RAM Legacy, but outcome is productivity regime shift (not abundance collapse) and design details (rolling window, origins, false positives on non-shifting stocks) are not visible in search results. Must be read in full before the novelty claim is finalized.

studies.citation: Cano AV, Jensen OP, Dakos V (2025) Identifying fish populations prone to abrupt shifts via dynamical footprint analysis. PNAS 122(34)
studies.data_system: 9,006 fish time series: 397 RAM Legacy productivity series, 199 ICES Atlantic cod CPUE series, 8,410 FishGlob CPUE series
studies.outcome_definition: Time-series shape classified as abrupt vs non-abrupt (linear, quadratic, no change), following the Pelissie et al. 2024 classification approach
studies.baseline_comparator: None visible; the 'dynamical footprint' (7 metrics: DEV, AR1, SD, dispersion, disparity, CV, skewness, computed on full series and in rolling windows) is the predictor; no state/trend forecasting baseline mentioned
studies.key_finding: Machine-learning classification of fish population time-series shapes from their dynamical footprint detects populations prone to abrupt shifts with 'moderate accuracy' across three datasets; 50 populations across 11 large marine ecosystems flagged as at risk of future abrupt shifts.
studies.notes: Directly overlaps the candidate data (RAM Legacy, FishGlob, ICES). Snippets describe whole-series classification rather than sequential forecast origins; accuracy metrics, cross-validation scheme and false-alarm rates are not visible in search results.

studies.citation: Pelissie M, Devictor V, Dakos V (2024) A systematic approach for detecting abrupt shifts in ecological timeseries. Biological Conservation
studies.data_system: Simulated series with varying noise/perturbations; applied to catch tonnage, bird index and insect occupancy time series
studies.outcome_definition: Trajectory classification into no change, linear, nonlinear (quadratic), abrupt; abrupt shifts confirmed by combining several existing methods
studies.key_finding: Provides a reproducible classifier for labelling abrupt shifts in ecological time series, with classification performance assessed on simulated data; code public.
studies.notes: Candidate outcome-labelling convention (used by Cano et al. 2025); not itself a forecasting study.

studies.citation: Litzow MA, Mueter FJ, Urban JD (2013) Rising catch variability preceded historical fisheries collapses in Alaska. Ecological Applications
studies.data_system: Spatially resolved catch data from Gulf of Alaska and Bering Sea crustacean fisheries; 12 collapsing fisheries plus non-collapsing fisheries
studies.outcome_definition: Stock collapse (operational threshold not visible in search results)
studies.baseline_comparator: Contrast with non-collapsing fisheries (no state/trend forecast model visible)
studies.key_finding: Spatial variability in catches increased 1-4 years before collapse; a random-effects model across 12 collapsing fisheries showed strong evidence of rising variability, and trends in variability differed significantly between collapsing and non-collapsing fisheries.
studies.notes: Retrospective, pooled (random-effects) test; per-series alarm rates or a calibrated false-alarm budget are not visible in search results.

studies.citation: Burthe SJ et al. (2016) Do early warning indicators consistently predict nonlinear change in long-term ecological data? Journal of Applied Ecology
studies.data_system: 55 taxa, 126 long-term datasets across trophic levels in marine and freshwater ecosystems
studies.outcome_definition: Statistically significant nonlinear abundance change in the series
studies.baseline_comparator: None (indicator presence cross-tabulated against nonlinear change)
studies.key_finding: True positives were uncommon (8% for variance, 6% for autocorrelation); variance and autocorrelation consistently failed to predict nonlinear change; 43% of series were categorised differently by variance vs autocorrelation.
studies.notes: Confusion-matrix style evaluation across transitioning and non-transitioning series, but retrospective on whole series; no sequential origins or state/trend baseline visible.

studies.citation: O'Brien DA, Deb S, Gal G, Thackeray SJ, Dutta PS, Matsuzaki SS, May L, Clements CF (2023) Early warning signals have limited applicability to empirical lake data. Nature Communications 14:7942
studies.data_system: Multi-trophic planktonic time series from multiple lakes around the world
studies.outcome_definition: Classified lake dynamics/abrupt change per trophic level; few instances met critical-transition criteria
studies.baseline_comparator: Chance (0.5) reliability; classic univariate vs multivariate EWS vs a machine-learning model (EWSNet)
studies.key_finding: Predictive ability was highly processing-dependent; most indicators performed no better than chance across true-positive and true-negative series; multivariate EWS weakly superior to univariate; a recent ML model performed poorly.
studies.notes: Directly relevant to the lake challenge analysis; explicitly evaluates non-transitioning (true negative) series. Sequential origins and a state/trend baseline are not visible.

studies.citation: Gsell AS, Scharfenberger U, Ozkundakci D, et al. (2016) Evaluating early-warning indicators of critical transitions in natural aquatic ecosystems. PNAS 113(50):E8089-E8095
studies.data_system: Long-term time series from five freshwater ecosystems with documented sudden, persistent transitions
studies.outcome_definition: Breakpoints in state-variable time series (sudden persistent transitions hypothesised to be critical transitions)
studies.key_finding: Four EWIs (AR1, SD, skewness, density ratio) showed mixed results and low detectability prior to identified breakpoints in five lakes.
studies.notes: Only transitioning systems appear to be analysed (per visible description); no false-alarm quantification visible.

studies.citation: Rohde E, Pearce NJT, Young J, Xenopoulos MA (2022) Applying early warning indicators to predict critical transitions in a lake undergoing multiple changes. Ecological Applications 32(7):e2685
studies.data_system: Lake Simcoe, Ontario (single lake recovering from eutrophication)
studies.outcome_definition: Breakpoints in state variables
studies.key_finding: Retrospectively evaluated agreement between SD, autocorrelation, skewness and kurtosis and breakpoints in state variables in a lake undergoing multiple changes; quantitative results not visible in search results.
studies.notes: Data on figshare (doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.19131815.v1 per snippet).

studies.citation: Buelo CD et al. (2022) Evaluating the performance of temporal and spatial early warning statistics of algal blooms. Ecological Applications
studies.data_system: Whole-lake experiments (algal blooms), temporal and spatial EWS
studies.outcome_definition: Algal bloom during experimental nutrient loading
studies.baseline_comparator: Alarm rates when the lake was not being pushed (reference periods/lake)
studies.key_finding: True-positive alarm rates were 2.5-8.3 times higher than false-positive rates for rolling-window SD; for rolling-window autocorrelation no variable had a higher true-positive than false-positive alarm rate; temporal EWS outperformed spatial EWS.
studies.notes: One of the few ecological EWS evaluations reporting explicit true- vs false-alarm rates; experimental lakes, not population collapse.

studies.citation: Wilkinson GM, Carpenter SR, Cole JJ, Pace ML, Batt RD, Buelo CD, Kurtzweil JT (2018) Early warning signals precede cyanobacterial blooms in multiple whole-lake experiments. Ecological Monographs 88:188-203
studies.data_system: Six whole-lake experimental nutrient additions with a reference ecosystem; blooms in 5 of 6 lake-years
studies.outcome_definition: Regime shift from clear-water to cyanobacteria-dominated state (bloom)
studies.baseline_comparator: Reference (unmanipulated) lake; 'quickest detection' sequential statistic flags when manipulated-lake indicators deviate from the reference
studies.key_finding: Rising SD and autocorrelation of algal pigments and dissolved oxygen were detected by a sequential quickest-detection method before blooms in whole-lake experiments; blooms occurred in five of six lake-years.
studies.notes: Sequential/online detection against a reference system is the closest ecological analogue to a prequential design, but at ecosystem (not population) scale. Author list from snippet may be partial.

studies.citation: Carpenter SR, Cole JJ, Pace ML, Batt R, Brock WA, Cline T, Coloso J, Hodgson JR, Kitchell JF, Seekell DA, Smith L, Weidel B (2011) Early warnings of regime shifts: a whole-ecosystem experiment. Science 332:1079-1082
studies.data_system: Manipulated lake (top predator addition over 3 years) with adjacent reference lake, high-frequency monitoring
studies.outcome_definition: Food-web regime shift
studies.key_finding: Warning signals (slowing return rates, rising variance) were evident in the manipulated lake more than a year before the food-web transition, with the reference lake as control.
studies.notes: Single manipulated vs single reference system.

studies.citation: Drake JM, Griffen BD (2010) Early warning signals of extinction in deteriorating environments. Nature 467:456-459
studies.data_system: Laboratory Daphnia magna populations (60 tanks; half with deteriorating food supply, half controls)
studies.outcome_definition: Extinction / crossing of tipping point under deteriorating environment
studies.key_finding: Four statistical indicators showed critical slowing down in deteriorating but not control populations, up to eight generations before extinction.
studies.notes: Experimental; control populations provide non-transitioning comparison.

studies.citation: Clements CF, Ozgul A (2016) Including trait-based early warning signals helps predict population collapse. Nature Communications 7:10984
studies.data_system: Microcosm experiment (abundance and body-size time series)
studies.outcome_definition: Population collapse / critical transition in experimental populations
studies.baseline_comparator: Abundance-only EWS vs composite abundance+trait indices
studies.key_finding: Composite indices including body-size dynamics gave more accurate inference of approaching collapse than abundance time series alone.
studies.notes: Evaluation metrics not visible in search results.

studies.citation: Clements CF, Drake JM, Griffiths JI, Ozgul A (2015) Factors influencing the detectability of early warning signals of population collapse. American Naturalist 186(1):50-58
studies.data_system: not visible in search results (paper notes most documented EWS are from controlled laboratory systems or models)
studies.outcome_definition: Population collapse
studies.key_finding: Examines factors (e.g., sampling/observation constraints) that influence detectability of EWS of collapse; specific results not visible in search results.
studies.notes: Design details not visible.

studies.citation: Clements CF, Blanchard JL, Nash KL, Hindell MA, Ozgul A (2017) Body size shifts and early warning signals precede the historic collapse of whale stocks. Nature Ecology & Evolution
studies.data_system: Historical whaling catch records (blue, fin, sei, sperm whales): abundance and body-size data
studies.outcome_definition: Global collapse of whale stocks (operational definition not visible)
studies.key_finding: Mean body size of caught whales declined by up to 4 m over 70 years; combined trait+abundance EWS detectable up to 40 years before global collapse.
studies.notes: Retrospective on collapsed stocks only (per visible description).

studies.citation: Clements CF, McCarthy MA, Blanchard JL (2019) Early warning signals of recovery in complex systems. Nature Communications 10:1681
studies.data_system: Trait-based ecological model plus real-world fisheries data (cod populations)
studies.outcome_definition: Recovery of overexploited stocks
studies.baseline_comparator: Abundance-only vs trait-only vs combined signals
studies.key_finding: Abundance- and trait-based signals were independently detectable before cod recovery; combining them gave the best predictions of recovery.
studies.notes: Recovery, not collapse.

studies.citation: Arkilanian AA, Clements CF, Ozgul A, Baruah G (2020) Effect of time series length and resolution on abundance- and trait-based early warning signals of population declines. Ecology
studies.data_system: Simulations (per snippet); empirical component not visible
studies.outcome_definition: Population decline/collapse in simulated populations
studies.key_finding: Abundance-based EWS require roughly 5-10 generations of data as a minimum; adding trait information halves the required length; no evident decrease in performance with coarser resolution.
studies.notes: Useful for prespecifying minimum series length.

studies.citation: Cerini F, Childs DZ, Clements CF (2023) A predictive timeline of wildlife population collapse. Nature Ecology & Evolution 7:320-331
studies.data_system: Conceptual framework (perspective); no new empirical evaluation visible
studies.outcome_definition: Population collapse; the search snippet from the related 2025 paper notes 80-90% declines are commonly used operational thresholds
studies.key_finding: Proposes a framework in which individual-level behavioural and morphological changes precede EWS and abundance declines, motivating multi-dimensional monitoring.
studies.notes: Framework paper; useful for outcome-definition conventions.

studies.citation: Cerini F et al. (2025) Multivariate signals of population collapse in a high-throughput ecological experiment. Ecology 106(9):e70197
studies.data_system: Autonomously monitored high-throughput Paramecium caudatum populations forced to collapse by a pollutant
studies.outcome_definition: Population collapse under increasing stress
studies.key_finding: A predictable sequence was observed: declines in movement speed, then body length, then emergence of EWS of collapse, and finally abundance declines.
studies.notes: AUC/ROC details not visible.

studies.citation: Hefley TJ, Tyre AJ, Blankenship EE (2013) Statistical indicators and state-space population models predict extinction in a population of bobwhite quail. Theoretical Ecology 6:319-331
studies.data_system: Wild bobwhite quail population in an agricultural region with habitat deterioration; two independent datasets
studies.outcome_definition: Transcritical-bifurcation extinction threshold (population crossing threshold estimated in 2010, 95% CI 2002-2036, in one dataset and 2008 in the other)
studies.baseline_comparator: State-space population model used alongside a statistical indicator to estimate threshold crossing
studies.key_finding: Both a statistical (EWS-type) indicator and state-space population models detected the extinction threshold in a wild population, one of the first field applications.
studies.notes: Directly pairs EWS with a state-space threshold-crossing forecast, but on a single population; no comparative skill evaluation visible.

studies.citation: Krkosek M, Drake JM (2014) On signals of phase transitions in salmon population dynamics. Proceedings of the Royal Society B 281:20133221
studies.data_system: Salmon population dynamics (specific series not visible)
studies.outcome_definition: Phase transition / bifurcation in salmon dynamics
studies.key_finding: Examines whether critical slowing down reveals EWS in salmon population dynamics; results not visible in search results.
studies.notes: Design details not visible.

studies.citation: Litzow MA, Hunsicker ME (2016) Early warning signals, nonlinearity, and signs of hysteresis in real ecosystems. Ecosphere 7:e01614
studies.data_system: Review/meta-analysis of published EWS studies plus eight northeast Pacific Ocean time series
studies.outcome_definition: Ecological transitions in published studies; nonlinearity/hysteresis tests
studies.key_finding: Published studies demonstrating nonlinear dynamics were more likely to support EWS predictions than studies with linear or undetermined dynamics; recommends testing for nonlinearity/hysteresis before applying EWS.
studies.notes: Supports grouping by system and pre-screening for dynamical regime.

studies.citation: [authors not visible] (2016) Elevated nonlinearity as indicator of transition to overexploitation in fish stocks. bioRxiv preprint
studies.data_system: Ricker-type simulations plus long-term fish time series from the Southern California Current and US Northeast Shelf
studies.outcome_definition: Transition to chaotic dynamics or abrupt shift to overexploited state
studies.key_finding: Variance and nonlinearity increase similarly in magnitude along both types of transition; discusses capacity of nonlinearity, variance and autocorrelation as early warnings.
studies.notes: Preprint; authors and peer-review status not visible in search results.

studies.citation: Bury TM, Sujith RI, Pavithran I, Scheffer M, Lenton TM, Anand M, Bauch CT (2021) Deep learning for early warning signals of tipping points. PNAS 118
studies.data_system: Trained on simulated bifurcation time series; tested on model data and empirical thermoacoustic-instability and paleoclimate transition data
studies.outcome_definition: Approach to a bifurcation (fold, Hopf, transcritical) vs null (no bifurcation)
studies.baseline_comparator: Variance and lag-1 autocorrelation (classical EWS), compared via ROC/AUC using 80-100% of the pre-transition series
studies.key_finding: A CNN-LSTM classifier trained only on simulated data outperformed variance and lag-1 autocorrelation (AUC) in anticipating transitions in held-out model and empirical data.
studies.notes: Author list per snippet may be incomplete; ROC-based comparison but not a fixed-horizon, false-alarm-budgeted population-collapse hindcast.

studies.citation: Bury TM et al. (2023) Predicting discrete-time bifurcations with deep learning. Nature Communications 14:6331
studies.data_system: Simulated discrete-time models (physiology, economics, ecology) and experimental chick-heart aggregate data
studies.outcome_definition: Five codimension-one discrete-time bifurcations
studies.baseline_comparator: Commonly used EWS (sensitivity and specificity compared)
studies.key_finding: Deep-learning classifier showed higher sensitivity and specificity than classical EWS across noise intensities and rates of approach.
studies.notes: Not population-abundance data.

studies.citation: Deb S, Sidheekh S, Clements CF, Krishnan NC, Dutta PS (2022) Machine learning methods trained on simple models can predict critical transitions in complex natural systems. Royal Society Open Science 9:211475
studies.data_system: Trained on time series simulated from nine dynamical models (catastrophic, non-catastrophic, no transition); tested on real-world climate and ecological population-collapse time series (6 of 8 climate series classified correctly)
studies.outcome_definition: Catastrophic vs non-catastrophic vs no transition
studies.baseline_comparator: Four classical ML classifiers (logistic regression, SVM, random forest, MLP) trained on trend statistics such as autocorrelation (generic-EWS-based classifiers)
studies.key_finding: EWSNet trained on simple models outperformed EWS-trend-based classifiers and reliably predicted observed real-world transitions from climate change to ecological population collapse.
studies.notes: Which ecological datasets were used and per-dataset false-alarm rates are not visible in search results. O'Brien et al. 2023 report EWSNet performed poorly on lake data.

studies.citation: Grziwotz F, Chang CW, Dakos V, et al. (2023) Anticipating the occurrence and type of critical transitions. Science Advances
studies.data_system: Three model time series (fold, period-doubling, Neimark-Sacker) and empirical cases from cell-level experiments to paleoclimate
studies.outcome_definition: Critical transition (bifurcation) and its type
studies.key_finding: Introduces the dynamical eigenvalue (DEV), estimated via empirical dynamic modelling, whose modulus approaches 1 near bifurcation and whose position indicates transition type; validated on models and empirical cases.
studies.notes: Used as one of seven footprint metrics in Cano et al. 2025.

studies.citation: Boettiger C, Hastings A (2012) Quantifying limits to detection of early warning for critical transitions. Journal of the Royal Society Interface 9(75):2527-2539
studies.data_system: Simulated systems approaching and not approaching transitions
studies.outcome_definition: Simulated critical transition vs stable null
studies.baseline_comparator: Null (stable) simulations; likelihood-ratio model-based indicator vs summary statistics
studies.key_finding: Introduced ROC-curve evaluation of EWS trading off missed events vs false alarms; for summary statistics a 5% false-positive rate often corresponded to only about 5% true-positive rate (no better than chance).
studies.notes: Methodological foundation for a false-alarm-budgeted comparison; simulation only.

studies.citation: Boettiger C, Hastings A (2012) Early warning signals and the prosecutor's fallacy. Proceedings of the Royal Society B 279(1748):4734
studies.data_system: Simulated systems that transitioned purely by chance (stochastic transitions)
studies.outcome_definition: Stochastic (noise-induced) transition
studies.key_finding: Conditionally selecting systems known to have transitioned inflates false-positive rates of common warning statistics; mining historical collapses without accounting for selection can produce spurious benchmarks.
studies.notes: Motivates including non-collapsing series and complete follow-up.

studies.citation: Laitinen V, Dakos V, Lahti L (2021) Probabilistic early warning signals. Ecology and Evolution 11(20):14101-14114
studies.data_system: Simulated time-varying AR(1) processes (empirical applications not visible)
studies.outcome_definition: Rising lag-1 autocorrelation
studies.key_finding: Provides a probabilistic formulation of time-varying AR(1) and a probabilistic detector of rising lag-1 autocorrelation (extended to multivariate in a 2022 preprint).
studies.notes: Candidate for a probabilistic EWS score variant.

studies.citation: O'Brien DA, Deb S, Sidheekh S, Krishnan NC, Dutta PS, Clements CF (2023) EWSmethods: an R package to forecast tipping points at the community level using early warning signals, resilience measures, and machine learning models. Ecography e06674
studies.data_system: Software (univariate and multivariate EWS; rolling and expanding windows; EWSNet interface)
studies.outcome_definition: n/a
studies.key_finding: Unified implementation of classical rolling-window and expanding-window EWS plus EWSNet; expanding-window form described as more robust.
studies.notes: Useful for prespecified, reproducible EWS computation.

studies.citation: Dakos V, Scheffer M, van Nes EH, Brovkin V, Petoukhov V, Held H (2008) Slowing down as an early warning signal for abrupt climate change. PNAS 105:14308-14312
studies.data_system: Paleoclimate records of abrupt climate change
studies.outcome_definition: Documented abrupt climate shifts
studies.baseline_comparator: 1,000 surrogate series (bootstrap and Fourier-spectrum surrogates) for Kendall tau trend significance
studies.key_finding: Established the rolling-window AR1 + Kendall tau + surrogate-significance convention; autocorrelation increased before all analysed abrupt climate shifts.
studies.notes: Source of the standard EWS scoring/significance convention to be prespecified.

studies.citation: Hastings A, Wysham DB (2010) Regime shifts in ecological systems can occur with no warning. Ecology Letters 13(4):464-472
studies.data_system: Theory/models
studies.outcome_definition: Regime shift
studies.key_finding: Shows classes of regime shifts that lack critical slowing down and hence occur without generic EWS.
studies.notes: Theoretical reason to expect misses for the EWS score.

studies.citation: Ditlevsen PD, Johnsen SJ (2010) Tipping points: early warning and wishful thinking. Geophysical Research Letters 37:L19703
studies.data_system: Ice-core records
studies.outcome_definition: Dansgaard-Oeschger-type abrupt shifts
studies.key_finding: Ice-core analysis excludes a bifurcation scenario for the studied shifts, implying noise-induced transitions with very limited predictability.
studies.notes: Background on stochastic transitions.

studies.citation: Holmes EE, Sabo JL, Viscido SV, Fagan WF (2007) A statistical approach to quasi-extinction forecasting. Ecology Letters
studies.data_system: Simulated population processes and real time series (identity of real series not visible); each series split into a 20-year parameterization period and 10-, 20- or 30-year forecast period
studies.outcome_definition: Quasi-extinction: decline to a critical threshold within the forecast period
studies.baseline_comparator: It is the baseline: diffusion-approximation (statistical) risk model; bias and precision of risk estimates assessed
studies.key_finding: Statistical (diffusion-approximation) models fit to 20-30 years of counts gave relatively unbiased quasi-extinction risk with confidence intervals considerably narrower than (0,1), even for noisy simulated processes with density dependence, species interactions and age structure.
studies.notes: Directly relevant convention for a state-and-trend threshold-crossing baseline validated out of sample; single split per series rather than sequential origins (per visible description).

studies.citation: Holmes EE, Fagan WF, Rango JJ, Folarin AJAS, Lippe JE, McIntyre NE (2005) Cross validation of quasi-extinction risks from real time series: an examination of diffusion approximation methods. NOAA Tech. Memo. NMFS-NWFSC-67
studies.data_system: Real population time series (identity not visible)
studies.outcome_definition: Quasi-extinction risk (decline to threshold)
studies.key_finding: Cross-validates diffusion-approximation quasi-extinction risk estimates against realised outcomes in real time series.
studies.notes: Details not visible beyond title and author list.

studies.citation: Sabo JL, Holmes EE, Kareiva PM (2004) Efficacy of simple viability models in ecological risk assessment: does density dependence matter? Ecology 85:328-341
studies.data_system: not visible in search results
studies.outcome_definition: Quasi-extinction risk
studies.baseline_comparator: Diffusion-approximation viability models with/without density dependence
studies.key_finding: Assesses whether accounting for density dependence changes the accuracy of simple viability models; extreme density dependence identified as a case where diffusion approximations perform poorly.
studies.notes: Design details not visible.

studies.citation: Ward EJ, Holmes EE, Thorson JT, Collen B (2014) Complexity is costly: a meta-analysis of parametric and non-parametric methods for short-term population forecasting. Oikos 123(6):652-661
studies.data_system: Time series of counts/survey data from RAM Legacy and GPDD (per reproduction report); 49 model parameterizations
studies.outcome_definition: Continuous abundance forecast (absolute scaled error), not collapse
studies.baseline_comparator: Naive last-observation (random walk) forecast vs low-dimensional autoregressive, Gompertz, state-space and non-parametric models
studies.key_finding: Low-dimensional parametric autoregressive models gave the most accurate short-term forecasts across taxa; the most accurate model simply used the most recent observation; complex parametric and non-parametric models did worse except for highly cyclic species.
studies.notes: Key convention for the state-and-trend baseline and for capacity matching; independent reproduction available (RREEBES).

studies.citation: Perretti CT, Munch SB, Sugihara G (2013) Model-free forecasting outperforms the correct mechanistic model for simulated and experimental data. PNAS 110(13):5253-5257
studies.data_system: Simulated noisy nonlinear systems and experimental time series
studies.outcome_definition: Continuous short-term forecast accuracy
studies.baseline_comparator: Correctly specified mechanistic model fit with common statistical techniques vs state-space-reconstruction (EDM) methods
studies.key_finding: State-space-reconstruction forecasts were most accurate even using a single series; a published critique (Hartig & Dormann) argued a simple modification of the statistical fitting removes the bias and reverses the result.
studies.notes: Cautionary evidence for baseline-fitting choices.

studies.citation: Ye H, Beamish RJ, Glaser SM, Grant SCH, Hsieh C, Richards LJ, Schnute JT, Sugihara G (2015) Equation-free mechanistic ecosystem forecasting using empirical dynamic modeling. PNAS 112(13):E1569-E1576
studies.data_system: Nine Fraser River sockeye salmon stocks
studies.outcome_definition: Continuous recruitment/return forecasts
studies.baseline_comparator: Ricker spawner-recruit models and extensions vs EDM formulations
studies.key_finding: EDM produced more accurate and precise out-of-sample forecasts than Ricker-based models and improved when environmental factors were included.
studies.notes: Fisheries out-of-sample forecasting convention.

studies.citation: Munch SB, Giron-Nava A, Sugihara G (2018) Nonlinear dynamics and noise in fisheries recruitment: a global meta-analysis. Fish and Fisheries 19:964-973
studies.data_system: Global database of 185 fish populations (recruitment/stock series)
studies.outcome_definition: Continuous recruitment prediction accuracy
studies.key_finding: EDM predicted recruitment more accurately than conventional stock-recruitment models about 90% of the time.
studies.notes: Author list per snippet is partial; leave-one-out details not visible in search results.

studies.citation: Glaser SM, Fogarty MJ, Liu H, Altman I, Hsieh C, Kaufman L, MacCall AD, Rosenberg AA, Ye H, Sugihara G (2014) Complex dynamics may limit prediction in marine fisheries. Fish and Fisheries 15:616-633
studies.data_system: Over 200 survey-abundance and landings time series from two ecosystems
studies.outcome_definition: Continuous forecast skill by horizon
studies.baseline_comparator: Nonlinear (EDM) forecasting models; linear comparison per method
studies.key_finding: Dynamics were predictable over a 1-year horizon in 70% of series but predictability declined exponentially over a 5-year horizon; fished species more often nonlinear; landings less predictable than abundance indices.
studies.notes: Author list per snippet may be incomplete; informs the 1-5 year horizon choice.

studies.citation: Pennekamp F, Iles AC, Garland J, et al. (2019) The intrinsic predictability of ecological time series and its potential to guide forecasting. Ecological Monographs 89:e01359
studies.data_system: Simulations plus 461 empirical ecological time series
studies.outcome_definition: Forecast error (continuous)
studies.baseline_comparator: Permutation entropy as a model-free predictability bound vs realised forecast error
studies.key_finding: Permutation entropy covaries with forecast error across simulations and 461 empirical series, separating intrinsic from realised predictability.
studies.notes: Potential covariate/stratifier for system-level forecastability.

studies.citation: Dietze MC, Fox A, Beck-Johnson LM, et al. (2018) Iterative near-term ecological forecasting: needs, opportunities, and challenges. PNAS 115(7):1424-1432
studies.data_system: Perspective (no empirical evaluation)
studies.outcome_definition: n/a
studies.key_finding: Argues for iterative near-term (daily to decadal) forecasts that are compared to new observations, with uncertainty quantification and cyberinfrastructure needs.
studies.notes: Framework justification for sequential, time-indexed evaluation.

studies.citation: Thomas RQ, Boettiger C, Carey CC, et al. (2023) The NEON Ecological Forecasting Challenge. Frontiers in Ecology and the Environment 21(3):112-113; and Olsson F, et al. (2025) What can we learn from 100,000 freshwater forecasts? A synthesis from the NEON Ecological Forecasting Challenge. Ecological Applications
studies.data_system: NEON site forecasts (freshwater and other themes) submitted by community teams
studies.outcome_definition: Continuous variables scored per site and horizon
studies.baseline_comparator: Null models: random walk and day-of-year climatology (normal distribution of historical observations); skill via CRPS relative to climatology over 1-30 day horizons
studies.key_finding: Establishes a community convention of proper scoring (CRPS via scoringRules/score4cast), evaluation at each horizon, and comparison against climatology and random-walk nulls; most models show increasing error with lead time.
studies.notes: Author lists per snippets are partial; provides the proper-scoring and null-baseline conventions.

studies.citation: Lewis ASL, Woelmer WM, Wander HL, et al. (2022) Increased adoption of best practices in ecological forecasting enables comparisons of forecastability. Ecological Applications 32:e2500
studies.data_system: Systematic review of 178 near-term (<=10-year horizon) ecological forecasting papers
studies.outcome_definition: n/a (review)
studies.key_finding: Adoption of best practices (data publication, forecast archiving, automation, null-model comparison) is increasing but remains low overall; enables cross-ecosystem comparison of forecastability.
studies.notes: Benchmark for reporting standards.

studies.citation: Harris DJ, Taylor SD, White EP (2018) Forecasting biodiversity in breeding birds using best practices. PeerJ 6:e4278
studies.data_system: North American Breeding Bird Survey; hindcasts evaluated annually for a decade at 1,237 sites
studies.outcome_definition: Species richness (continuous)
studies.baseline_comparator: Simple baselines (e.g., average/naive) among six modelling approaches
studies.key_finding: Hindcasting six approaches against baselines showed simple baselines are hard to beat; codifies best practices (hindcasting, archiving, baseline comparison, uncertainty).
studies.notes: Template for sequential hindcast evaluation.

studies.citation: White EP, Yenni GM, Taylor SD, Christensen EM, Bledsoe EK, Simonis JL, Ernest SKM (2019) Developing an automated iterative near-term forecasting system for an ecological study. Methods in Ecology and Evolution
studies.data_system: Portal Project rodent abundances (>40 years monthly data)
studies.outcome_definition: Continuous abundance forecasts 12 months ahead
studies.baseline_comparator: Multiple models compared by RMSE and interval coverage; models with vs without multispecies dependencies
studies.key_finding: Rolling hindcasts (fit to a date, forecast 12 months) allow many model comparisons; models capturing multispecies dependencies gave superior hindcasts and forecasts.
studies.notes: Rolling-origin hindcast convention with coverage as calibration metric.

studies.citation: Petchey OL, Pontarp M, Massie TM, Kefi S, Ozgul A, et al. (2015) The ecological forecast horizon, and examples of its uses and determinants. Ecology Letters 18:597-611
studies.data_system: Five case studies (models/experiments)
studies.outcome_definition: Forecast proficiency vs a 'good enough' threshold
studies.key_finding: Defines the forecast horizon as the distance over which forecasts remain useful, requiring a target variable, a proficiency measure and a proficiency threshold; revisited by Wesselkamp et al. 2025 (MEE) as potential/absolute/relative predictability.
studies.notes: Conceptual basis for choosing 1-5 year horizons.

studies.citation: Roberts DR, Bahn V, Ciuti S, Boyce MS, Elith J, Guillera-Arroita G, et al. (2017) Cross-validation strategies for data with temporal, spatial, hierarchical, or phylogenetic structure. Ecography 40(8):913-929
studies.data_system: Methodological review with simulations/examples
studies.outcome_definition: n/a
studies.key_finding: Ignoring temporal/spatial/hierarchical structure in cross-validation seriously underestimates predictive error; block cross-validation is nearly universally more appropriate when predicting to new data.
studies.notes: Justifies grouping by biological system in holdouts.

studies.citation: Pinsky ML, Jensen OP, Ricard D, Palumbi SR (2011) Unexpected patterns of fisheries collapse in the world's oceans. PNAS 108(20):8317-8322
studies.data_system: 223 scientific stock assessments for 120 species (RAM-type assessment database) plus FAO landings 1950-2006
studies.outcome_definition: Stock collapsed if minimum annual biomass fell below 20% of BMSY
studies.key_finding: Up to twice as many fisheries for small, low-trophic-level species collapsed as for large predators; provides a widely used assessment-based collapse definition (Bmin < 0.2 BMSY).
studies.notes: Candidate collapse definition for RAM Legacy; follow-up Pinsky & Byler 2015 (Proc B) links fishing, fast growth and climate variability to collapse risk.

studies.citation: Vert-pre KA, Amoroso RO, Jensen OP, Hilborn R (2013) Frequency and intensity of productivity regime shifts in marine fish stocks. PNAS 110(5):1779-1784
studies.data_system: Marine fish stock assessments (RAM-type; specific count not visible)
studies.outcome_definition: Productivity (surplus production) regime shifts between low and high regimes
studies.key_finding: First quantitative assessment of frequency and intensity of productivity regime shifts across marine stocks; generated methodological debate (Szuwalski critique and reply).
studies.notes: Outcome-definition source for the productivity-shift outcome used by Zhang 2020.

studies.citation: Free CM, Jensen OP, Anderson SC, et al. (2020) Blood from a stone: performance of catch-only methods in estimating stock biomass status. Fisheries Research 223
studies.data_system: Data-rich RAM Legacy stocks and simulated fisheries
studies.outcome_definition: B/BMSY status classes
studies.baseline_comparator: 11 catch-only methods compared as classifiers of status
studies.key_finding: Catch-only methods gave imprecise and biased B/BMSY estimates and were poor status classifiers, except a superensemble ('fair' on simulations) and refined ORCS ('good' on RAM Legacy stocks).
studies.notes: Illustrates classifier-evaluation conventions on RAM Legacy (status, not collapse timing).

studies.citation: Collen B, McRae L, Deinet S, De Palma A, et al. (2011) Predicting how populations decline to extinction. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B 366(1577):2577-2586
studies.data_system: Mammalian population trend data from the largest repository of abundance trends (Living Planet-type data) combined with PanTHERIA traits
studies.outcome_definition: Decline in mammalian abundance
studies.key_finding: Asks which factors predict decline in mammalian abundance using trait and trend data.
studies.notes: Trait-based, not EWS; validation design not visible.

studies.citation: Wauchope HS, Amano T, Sutherland WJ, Johnston A (2019) When can we trust population trends? A method for quantifying the effects of sampling interval and duration. Methods in Ecology and Evolution 10:2067-2078
studies.data_system: Waterbird abundance time series
studies.outcome_definition: Trend direction/magnitude reliability
studies.key_finding: Short series unlikely to match true trend magnitude but tend to reflect trend direction; at least ~10 years recommended to reliably detect trends; LPI sensitivity to series length noted.
studies.notes: Informs minimum-length filters for LPD/GPDD series.

studies.citation: [authors not visible] (2026) Early Warning Signals in Ecological Time-Series. Entropy 28(6):628
studies.data_system: Review (theory, indicators, empirical applications across lakes, coral reefs, grasslands, forests, fisheries)
studies.outcome_definition: n/a
studies.key_finding: Synthesises EWS methods; reports that rolling windows generally outperform expanding windows on simulated and empirical series; states prospective monitoring of non-transitioning systems is essential to assess false-positive rates; notes Allee-driven fish dynamics may show 'critical speeding up' (decreasing variance/AC).
studies.notes: Recent review useful for positioning; authors not visible in search results.

studies.citation: Dakos V, Boulton CA, Buxton JE, et al. (2024) Tipping point detection and early warnings in climate, ecological, and human systems. Earth System Dynamics 15:1117
studies.data_system: Review
studies.outcome_definition: n/a
studies.key_finding: Cross-domain review of tipping-point detection and EWS; content details not visible in search results.
studies.notes: Author list beyond first author not visible.

studies.citation: Clements CF, Ozgul A (2018) Indicators of transitions in biological systems. Ecology Letters
studies.data_system: Review
studies.outcome_definition: n/a
studies.key_finding: Review of abundance- and trait-based indicators of transitions in biological systems; details not visible in search results.
studies.notes: Background.

studies.citation: Lapeyrolerie M, Boettiger C (2023) Limits to ecological forecasting: estimating uncertainty for critical transitions with deep learning. Methods in Ecology and Evolution 14:785-798
studies.data_system: Simulated classic ecological models with critical transitions
studies.outcome_definition: Probabilistic forecast of trajectories through critical transitions
studies.key_finding: Probabilistic deep-learning forecasters were compared with MCMC and autoregressive forecasts on simulated critical transitions, emphasising informative uncertainty over point forecasts.
studies.notes: Simulation only; relevant to capacity-matched learner design.

notes: Tool limits: WebSearch only; WebFetch/curl not attempted given the stated egress block, so all design fields come from search-result snippets (abstract-level), which is why many fields are 'unknown'. 82 distinct queries run. Key sweep conclusions: (1) No study surfaced that combines sequential fixed-horizon origins + out-of-sample holdout + matched state/trend baseline + false-alarm-budget calibration + complete follow-up for population-abundance collapse across realms; the closest fisheries-wide EWS hindcasts are Zhang 2020 (Ecological Indicators; SD/AR1 vs productivity regime shifts in 191 RAM Legacy populations; >5-year lead for >50% of populations) and Cano, Jensen & Dakos 2025 (PNAS; ML on 'dynamical footprint' across 9,006 RAM Legacy/ICES cod/FishGlob series, 'moderate accuracy'), both of which must be read in full before the novelty statement is finalized (their handling of origins, false alarms and baselines is not visible). (2) Prior work clearly did NOT ignore false positives or non-transitioning series: Burthe 2016 (TP 8%/6%), O'Brien 2023 (true-negative series; most indicators at chance), Buelo 2022 (TP:FP ratios), Litzow 2013 (non-collapsing fisheries), Boettiger & Hastings 2012 (ROC; prosecutor's fallacy), Drake & Griffen 2010 and Carpenter 2011 (controls/reference lakes) — consistent with the project's stated non-claim. (3) Sequential/online detection exists at ecosystem scale (Wilkinson 2018 'quickest detection' vs reference lake) but not for population-collapse hindcasts. (4) Hefley 2013 pairs an EWS indicator with a state-space threshold-crossing model on one quail population but without comparative skill evaluation. (5) Baseline/forecast conventions found: Ward 2014 (naive last-value/AR best on RAM Legacy+GPDD), Holmes 2007/2005 (diffusion-approximation quasi-extinction risk validated on held-out 10-30-yr forecast windows), NEON challenge (CRPS vs climatology/random-walk nulls per horizon), Harris 2018 and White 2019 (rolling hindcasts vs baselines), Roberts 2017 (block CV), Glaser 2014 (predictability decays by 5-year horizon). (6) Outcome-definition sources: Pinsky 2011 (Bmin<0.2 BMSY), Vert-pre 2013 (productivity regimes), Pelissie 2024 (abrupt-shift classifier), Cerini 2023/2025 (80-90% decline conventions mentioned in snippet). (7) No study on Living Planet Database or BioTIME using EWS or out-of-sample collapse hindcasts surfaced in any query; GPDD appears only via Ward 2014 (forecasting) and Cano 2025 does not use it. (8) Author lists for several entries are partial as shown in snippets (flagged in notes); no DOIs were invented — where the DOI was not visible, a landing-page URL is given instead. No EWS-outcome associations were computed.
