studies.citation: Bury, T.M. et al. (2021) Deep learning for early warning signals of tipping points. PNAS 118(39): e2106140118 (full co-author list not visible in search results)
studies.data_system: CNN-LSTM classifier trained on a large library of simulated models (fold, Hopf, transcritical bifurcations); tested on ecological model simulations and on empirical series: Mediterranean sedimentary archive (marine anoxic events), thermoacoustic instability experiments, and rate-of-change experiments (visible in snippets)
studies.outcome_definition: Approach to a bifurcation in models; documented transitions in empirical series (exact empirical labelling rule not visible in search results)
studies.baseline_comparator: Classical EWS only: variance and lag-1 autocorrelation; AR(1) null/surrogate series (10 per empirical series) used as negatives. No state-or-trend forecasting baseline visible.
studies.key_finding: Snippets state the DL classifier is more sensitive and generates fewer false positives than generic indicators, with ROC curves/AUC computed for predictions using 80-100% of the pre-transition series on model and empirical data (specific AUC values not visible in search results).
studies.notes: Evaluation is fraction-of-pre-transition-series based rather than fixed calendar horizon; negatives are AR(1) surrogates rather than observed non-transitioning ecological populations. Dablander & Bury 2022 later showed the classifier learned detrending-filter-specific features. No ecological population abundance databases (RAM, GPDD, LPD) visible in results.

studies.citation: Dablander, F. & Bury, T.M. (2022) Deep learning for tipping points: Preprocessing matters. PNAS (letter); with Bury et al. reply 'Dealing with the unknown unknowns of deep learning'
studies.data_system: Re-analysis of the Bury et al. 2021 classifier (simulated training data); preprocessing/detrending experiments
studies.outcome_definition: Not applicable (methodological critique)
studies.baseline_comparator: Classical EWS (variance, lag-1 AC) discussed for comparison of detrending sensitivity
studies.key_finding: The Bury et al. 2021 deep learning classifier learned not only generic bifurcation features but features specific to the detrending filter used on all training examples, so a particular detrending is required at test time; classical indicators need adequate detrending to avoid bias. Reply (PNAS 2022, DOI 10.1073/pnas.2210407119) frames this as an 'unknown unknowns' issue of DL.
studies.notes: Directly relevant to the preregistration decision to fix preprocessing a priori for both EWS and learners.

studies.citation: Bury, T.M., Dylewsky, D., Bauch, C.T., Anand, M., Glass, L., Shrier, A. & Bub, G. (2023) Predicting discrete-time bifurcations with deep learning. Nature Communications
studies.data_system: Classifier trained on simulations of the five codimension-one discrete-time bifurcations; tested on discrete-time models from physiology, economics and ecology and on experimental chick-heart aggregate data (period-doubling)
studies.outcome_definition: Approach to a discrete-time local bifurcation (model) / observed period-doubling in chick-heart aggregates
studies.baseline_comparator: Commonly used EWS (variance, lag-1 autocorrelation); no state/trend forecasting baseline visible
studies.key_finding: Snippets report higher sensitivity and specificity than commonly used EWS across a wide range of noise intensities and rates of approach to the bifurcation.
studies.notes: Empirical test is a physiological experiment, not ecological population data. Discrete-time focus is relevant to annual population indices.

studies.citation: Deb, S., Sidheekh, S., Clements, C.F., Krishnan, N.C. & Dutta, P.S. (2022) Machine learning methods trained on simple models can predict critical transitions in complex natural systems (EWSNet). Royal Society Open Science 9(2): 211475
studies.data_system: LSTM+FCN network (EWSNet) trained on simulated data (Dataset-W, Dataset-C); applied to real-world transitions 'from rapid climatic change to the collapse of ecological populations' (specific empirical series not visible in search results)
studies.outcome_definition: Three classes: catastrophic transition, non-catastrophic/smooth transition, no transition
studies.baseline_comparator: Comparison to classical EWS not visible in search results (unknown); no state/trend baseline visible
studies.key_finding: Mean test accuracy 99.46% (Dataset-W) and 95.93% (Dataset-C) on simulated test sets; error analysis reports no-transition series always classified correctly, 1% of catastrophic mislabelled non-catastrophic and 8% of non-catastrophic mislabelled catastrophic (Dataset-C). Claims reliable prediction of observed real-world transitions.
studies.notes: O'Brien et al. 2023 (Nat Commun) later found EWSNet's true-negative rate on empirical lake data was very low (0.06-0.2). EWSNet is exposed via the EWSmethods R package.

studies.citation: Lapeyrolerie, M. & Boettiger, C. (2023) Limits to ecological forecasting: Estimating uncertainty for critical transitions with deep learning. Methods in Ecology and Evolution 14(3): 785-798
studies.data_system: Simulated only: three examples (Hopf bifurcation, saddle-node bifurcation, stochastic transition) with probabilistic deep-learning time-series forecasters
studies.outcome_definition: Simulated critical transitions (bifurcation or noise-induced)
studies.key_finding: Frames critical transitions as forecasting problems requiring informative uncertainty rather than point forecasts; concludes that because never-before-observed behaviour is hard to forecast quantitatively, research should focus more on the qualitative predictions emphasized in the EWS/resilience literature.
studies.notes: Probabilistic-forecast framing (uncertainty estimation) is adjacent to calibration; no empirical ecological data visible. Companion PNAS 2021 commentary 'Teaching machines to anticipate catastrophes' (https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2115605118) by the same authors discusses Bury et al. 2021.

studies.citation: Grziwotz, F., Chang, C.-W., Dakos, V., van Nes, E., Schwarzländer, M., Kamps, O., Heßler, M., Tokuda, I., Telschow, A. & Hsieh, C.-h. (2023) Anticipating the occurrence and type of critical transitions. Science Advances 9: eabq4558
studies.data_system: Dynamical eigenvalue (DEV) estimated via S-map (empirical dynamic modeling, lag-embedding); model systems with known bifurcations plus five empirical datasets (identities not visible in search results)
studies.outcome_definition: |DEV| approaching 1 indicates approach to bifurcation; position in complex plane classifies fold vs period-doubling vs Neimark-Sacker
studies.key_finding: Introduces DEV as an EWS rooted in bifurcation theory that anticipates both occurrence and type of transition; demonstrated on models and five empirical datasets with data and analysis documentation available.
studies.notes: EDM-based multivariate/state-space indicator; potential alternative 'capacity-matched' EWS but is not part of the prespecified classical score.

studies.citation: Kulkarni, K., Deb, S. & Dutta, P.S. (2024) Efficacy of dynamic eigenvalue in anticipating and distinguishing tipping points. Theoretical Ecology (bioRxiv 2024.01.09.574944)
studies.data_system: Model systems with known bifurcation types and some real-world critical transitions (details not visible in search results)
studies.outcome_definition: not visible in search results
studies.key_finding: Follow-up assessing the efficacy of DEV for anticipating and distinguishing tipping types; snippets only restate the DEV concept, so quantitative findings are not visible in search results.
studies.notes: Low detail; treat as a pointer for the DEV literature.

studies.citation: Weinans, E., Lever, J.J., Bathiany, S., Quax, R., Bascompte, J., van Nes, E.H., Scheffer, M. & van de Leemput, I.A. (2019) Finding the direction of lowest resilience in multivariate complex systems. Journal of the Royal Society Interface 16(159): 20190629
studies.data_system: Multivariate time series (simulation-based method comparison; empirical data use not visible in search results)
studies.outcome_definition: Direction of minimal resilience (slowest-recovering set of nodes) rather than a discrete collapse event
studies.baseline_comparator: Autocorrelation-based vs variance-based multivariate methods compared against each other
studies.key_finding: Natural fluctuations in multivariate series reveal slow network regions; the autocorrelation-based method is less robust for short/low-resolution series but more robust to varying noise levels than the variance-based method.
studies.notes: Foundational multivariate-indicator paper; not a collapse-prediction evaluation.

studies.citation: Weinans, E., Quax, R., van Nes, E.H. & van de Leemput, I.A. (2021) Evaluating the performance of multivariate indicators of resilience loss. Scientific Reports 11: 9148
studies.data_system: Evaluation of proposed multivariate extensions of resilience indicators (data used not visible in search results; abstract describes indicators for multivariate time series)
studies.outcome_definition: Approach to a tipping point via critical slowing down (details not visible)
studies.baseline_comparator: Univariate resilience indicators (implied by framing; details not visible)
studies.key_finding: Systematically compares multivariate resilience-loss indicators (extensions of univariate CSD indicators) for multivariate time series; frequently cited as the reference evaluation of multivariate EWS performance.
studies.notes: Performance details (which indicator wins under which conditions) are not visible in search results.

studies.citation: Chen, S., O'Dea, E.B., Drake, J.M. & Epureanu, B.I. (2019) Eigenvalues of the covariance matrix as early warning signals for critical transitions in ecological systems. Scientific Reports 9: 2572
studies.data_system: Multiple time series (ecological model context; empirical data use not visible in search results)
studies.outcome_definition: Approach to critical transition (largest covariance eigenvalue increases)
studies.key_finding: Proposes the largest eigenvalue of the covariance matrix (and its share of total variation) as multivariate EWS that increase under certain conditions as a system approaches a critical transition.
studies.notes: Method paper; three eigenvalue estimation methods compared (figure caption visible).

studies.citation: Laitinen, V. & Lahti, L. (2022) Probabilistic Multivariate Early Warning Signals. In: Computational Methods in Systems Biology (CMSB 2022), Springer; and Laitinen, Dakos & Lahti (2021) Probabilistic early warning signals. Ecology and Evolution
studies.data_system: Multivariate time series framing (microbiome to financial markets); specific datasets not visible in search results
studies.outcome_definition: not visible in search results
studies.key_finding: A probabilistic data-aggregation strategy is argued to improve early-warning detection by using multivariate information more efficiently; extends the earlier probabilistic (Bayesian) univariate EWS framework.
studies.notes: Probabilistic outputs are relevant to calibration-style evaluation, but no evaluation details visible.

studies.citation: O'Brien, D.A., Deb, S., Gal, G., Thackeray, S.J., Dutta, P.S., Matsuzaki, S.S., May, L. & Clements, C.F. (2023) Early warning signals have limited applicability to empirical lake data. Nature Communications (preprint title: 'Early warning signals are hampered by a lack of critical transitions in empirical lake data')
studies.data_system: Multitrophic long-term monitoring data from lakes around the world (monthly and yearly resolution); univariate and multivariate EWS plus pretrained EWSNet
studies.outcome_definition: Abrupt non-linear community change / critical transitions classified per trophic level (specific classification procedure not visible)
studies.baseline_comparator: Chance (null) performance; univariate vs multivariate EWS vs EWSNet compared; no state/trend forecasting baseline visible
studies.key_finding: Few critical transitions found; most indicators did not perform better than chance; multivariate EWS only weakly superior to univariate; EWSNet had high true-positive probabilities (0.92 monthly, 0.88 yearly) but very low true-negative probabilities (0.2 and 0.06); results strongly dependent on data preprocessing with no coherence across indicators.
studies.notes: Closest existing empirical test of ML + multivariate EWS on ecological monitoring data with explicit true-negative reporting; lake community rather than population-collapse outcome. Also notes EWSNet is univariate-only and was retrained for variable-length series.

studies.citation: O'Brien, D.A., Deb, S., Sidheekh, S., Krishnan, N.C., Sharathi Dutta, P. & Clements, C.F. (2023) EWSmethods: an R package to forecast tipping points at the community level using early warning signals, resilience measures, and machine learning models. Ecography e06674
studies.data_system: Software (R package); rolling and expanding window univariate/multivariate EWS; interface to Python EWSNet and S-EWSNet
studies.outcome_definition: not applicable (software)
studies.key_finding: Provides unified syntax for univariate and multivariate EWS with rolling-window and 'more robust' expanding-window calculation and an interface to EWSNet probabilities of sudden vs smooth transition.
studies.notes: Useful implementation reference for expanding-window (time-indexed) EWS computation.

studies.citation: Deb, S., Mahendru, E., Goyal, P., Guttal, V., Dutta, P.S. & Krishnan, N.C. (2024) Optimal sampling of spatial patterns improves deep learning-based early warning signals of critical transitions (S-EWSNet). Royal Society Open Science 11(6): 231767
studies.data_system: Spatial patterns from a stochastic cellular automata model; deep network (S-EWSNet) trained with optimal sampling strategy
studies.outcome_definition: Spatio-temporal critical transition (sudden vs smooth)
studies.key_finding: Optimal sampling of spatial patterns lets a deep network learn latent features of spatio-temporal transitions; S-EWSNet offered as a spatial EWS toolkit.
studies.notes: Spatial rather than population-time-series; not applicable to abundance-only datasets.

studies.citation: Dylewsky, D., Lenton, T.M., Scheffer, M., Bury, T.M., Fletcher, C.G., Anand, M. & Bauch, C.T. (2023) Universal early warning signals of phase transitions in climate systems. Journal of the Royal Society Interface 20(201): 20220562
studies.data_system: CNN-LSTM trained exclusively on 2D Ising model phase transitions; tested on real and simulated climate systems
studies.outcome_definition: Approaching phase transition (binary classification)
studies.key_finding: Proof of concept that a classifier trained only on Ising-model transitions transfers to climate time series with and without approaching transitions.
studies.notes: Climate, not ecological populations; illustrates sim-to-real transfer claims.

studies.citation: Ma, Z., Zeng, C., Zhang, Y.-C. & Bury, T.M. (2025) Predicting critical transitions with machine learning trained on surrogates of historical data. Communications Physics 8: 258
studies.data_system: Surrogate-data-based ML (SDML) trained on surrogates of past transitions; empirical/experimental data from geology, climatology, sociology and cardiology
studies.outcome_definition: Historical transitions in each system (definition per system not visible)
studies.baseline_comparator: Variance and lag-1 autocorrelation; no state/trend forecasting baseline visible
studies.key_finding: Training on surrogates of historical transitions removes the local-bifurcation assumption; reported higher sensitivity and specificity than variance and lag-1 AC across four empirical domains.
studies.notes: Training on system-specific history is a design alternative to sim-trained classifiers; no ecological population data visible in results.

studies.citation: Huang, Y., Bathiany, S., Ashwin, P. et al. (2024) Deep learning for predicting rate-induced tipping. Nature Machine Intelligence 6: 1556-1565
studies.data_system: Three prototypical simulated systems for rate-induced tipping with equilibrium drift and noise
studies.outcome_definition: Rate-induced transition probability
studies.key_finding: Deep learning framework predicts transition probabilities ahead of rate-induced tipping (where CSD-based EWS are not expected to work), with explainable-AI fingerprints even at long lead times.
studies.notes: Relevant caveat: CSD-based EWS are not designed for rate-induced transitions, which may be common in harvested populations.

studies.citation: Zhuge, C., Li, J. & Chen, W. (2024) Deep learning for predicting the occurrence of tipping points. arXiv:2407.18693
studies.data_system: 2D-CNN + LSTM trained using normal forms; regularly and irregularly sampled model time series; 'untrained systems'
studies.outcome_definition: Occurrence of a tipping point (bifurcation)
studies.baseline_comparator: Traditional bifurcation-theory EWS methods (details not visible)
studies.key_finding: Claims to outperform traditional methods on regularly sampled model series and to handle irregularly sampled data, a common feature of real-world series.
studies.notes: Preprint; empirical ecological application not visible.

studies.citation: Babazadeh Maghsoodlo, Y., Anand, M. & Bauch, C.T. (2025) Echoes Before Collapse: Deep Learning Detection of Flickering in Complex Systems. arXiv:2509.04683
studies.data_system: CNN-LSTM trained on synthetic series from polynomial functions with additive noise; tested on unseen stochastic systems and empirical dormouse body-temperature records and African Humid Period palaeoclimate proxies
studies.outcome_definition: Presence of flickering (bimodal switching) preceding regime shifts
studies.key_finding: Models trained on simplified dynamics generalize to diverse stochastic systems and detect flickering in empirical datasets.
studies.notes: Flickering is an EWS mechanism distinct from CSD; complement to the classical score.

studies.citation: Sevinchan, Y. and 10 others (2026) In-context learning to predict critical transitions in dynamical systems (TipPFN). arXiv:2605.12308
studies.data_system: Transformer prior-data fitted network trained on synthetic generator combining canonical bifurcation scenarios with randomized high-dimensional stochastic dynamics; tested on unseen tipping regimes, sim-to-real examples and real-world observations (identities not visible)
studies.outcome_definition: Relative distance to criticality (RDTC) regression
studies.baseline_comparator: Conventional statistical/spectral indicators (variance etc.) and existing deep-learning classifiers (per abstract framing)
studies.key_finding: Claims robust, state-of-the-art early detection in previously unseen tipping regimes, including zero-shot on real-world data, and argues existing DL classifiers do not extrapolate beyond their training distribution.
studies.notes: Most recent foundation-model-style approach found; ecological population application not visible.

studies.citation: Falmagne, G., Stephenson, A.B. & Levin, S.A. (2026) Interpretable early warnings using machine learning in an online game-experiment. PNAS 123(1): e2503493122
studies.data_system: Reddit r/place 2022 (training) and 2023 (test) game-experiment; gradient-boosted decision trees on multiple system-specific time series with memory-retaining features; SHAP interpretation
studies.outcome_definition: Transitions in human behavioural system (definition not visible)
studies.baseline_comparator: Standard early warning indicators (CSD-type); reported as significantly outperformed
studies.key_finding: Detects half of transitions within 20 minutes at a 3.6% false positive rate on 2022 data with performance robust on the held-out 2023 event; SHAP reveals critical slowing down or speeding up, lack of innovation/coordination, turbulent histories.

notes: Search limitations: per instructions, no WebFetch/curl attempts were made; all facts come from WebSearch result snippets, so design fields are frequently 'unknown' and some author lists are marked as not visible. Key takeaways for the novelty claim: (1) No search result showed a pretrained deep-learning EWS classifier (Bury 2021/2023, EWSNet, TipPFN, SDML) evaluated on population-abundance collapse in RAM Legacy, GPDD, Living Planet or BioTIME with a fixed calendar horizon, sequential origins, and complete follow-up; the closest empirical ecological test is O'Brien et al. 2023 (Nat Commun) on lake community data, which reported EWSNet true-negative rates of 0.06-0.2 and multivariate EWS only weakly better than univariate. (2) False positives ARE quantified in several ML papers (Bury 2021 AUC/ROC vs AR(1) nulls; Bury 2023 and Ma et al. 2025 sensitivity/specificity; Falmagne et al. 2026 FPR 3.6% with held-out year; Masuda 2026 low FPR), so the preregistration should not claim prior work ignored false alarms. (3) None of the visible results used a state-and-trend forecasting baseline (current abundance vs reference, recent slope, state-space threshold crossing); comparators were classical EWS, surrogate nulls, chance, or other ML methods. (4) Dablander & Bury 2022 shows DL classifiers can learn detrending-filter artefacts, supporting fixing preprocessing a priori. (5) The 2026 preprints (TipPFN; Zhai et al. on Transformer failure; Li et al. reservoir computing) indicate active but simulation-heavy development; ecological population applications were not visible. Queries 14, 36 and 47 (targeting RAM Legacy/GPDD/LPD/fish-stock applications of pretrained classifiers) returned no matching empirical study.

studies.citation: Boettiger C & Hastings A (2012) Quantifying limits to detection of early warning for critical transitions. Journal of The Royal Society Interface 9(75):2527-2539
studies.baseline_comparator: null model: simulated replicates from a stable (non-transitioning) system used to characterize false-alarm rates; model-based likelihood indicator compared against summary-statistic indicators
studies.data_system: simulations (stochastic models of a system approaching a saddle-node bifurcation vs a stable null); no empirical population data visible in search results
studies.outcome_definition: approach to a critical (bifurcation) transition in simulated models; not visible in detail
studies.key_finding: Frames EWS evaluation in terms of error rates (false alarms vs missed warnings) and shows error rates 'can be quite severe for common indicators even under favorable assumptions', while model-based indicators improve performance. A related snippet (appearing under the first query, apparently from the arXiv version) states that with summary statistics a 5% false-positive rate often corresponds to only ~5% true-positive rate, no better than a coin flip.
studies.notes: Directly relevant to the benchmark's explicit false-alarm budget and ROC-style calibration. The 'coin flip' quote was shown in a search summary without a clearly attributed source; treat as medium-confidence attribution.

studies.citation: Boettiger C & Hastings A (2012) Early warning signals and the prosecutor's fallacy. Proceedings of the Royal Society B 279(1748):4734-4739
studies.baseline_comparator: null model: simulated purely stochastic (non-bifurcation) transitions, then conditioning on those that happened to transition
studies.data_system: simulations
studies.outcome_definition: a stochastic (chance) transition between basins in a model with no bifurcation
studies.key_finding: Identifies a 'critical difference between selecting systems for study based on observing a critical transition and those systems for which one wishes to forecast the approach of a transition'; this conditional selection introduces bias (the prosecutor's fallacy), so retrospectively chosen transitioning series can show spurious EWS trends.
studies.notes: The canonical statement of outcome-conditioning/selection bias for EWS; supports the benchmark's requirement to include non-transitioning series and to fix forecast origins prospectively.

studies.citation: Boettiger C & Hastings A (2013) No early warning signals for stochastic transitions: insights from large deviation theory. Proceedings of the Royal Society B 280(1766):20131372
studies.baseline_comparator: theory (large deviation theory) and simulation; a reply to Drake (2013) 'Early warning signals of stochastic switching' (Proc R Soc B)
studies.data_system: theory and simulations
studies.outcome_definition: noise-induced (stochastic) switching between attractors without a bifurcation
studies.key_finding: Conditioning on observing a purely stochastic transition can generate trajectories that could be mistaken for an EWS of a critical transition when the shift is merely due to chance; later work cited in the snippet supports that unstable states are traversed too quickly for characteristic slowing down to appear.
studies.notes: Drake (2013) is only referenced in snippets (no DOI visible); it argued the opposite position. Together they define the N-tipping limitation: stochastic-driven collapses may carry no CSD signal, which bounds achievable recall for any EWS score.

studies.key_finding: Shows 'the class of ecological systems that will exhibit leading indicators of regime shifts is limited' and that there is a set of ecological models, and likely a class of natural systems, 'for which there will be no forewarning of a regime change'.
studies.notes: Foundational no-warning result; motivates reporting the fraction of collapses that are in principle undetectable by CSD-based scores.

studies.notes: The predominance of positive case studies in the literature is itself relevant to publication/selection bias concerns raised in other entries.

studies.citation: Authors not visible in search results (2026) Early Warning Signals in Ecological Time-Series. Entropy 28(6):628
studies.data_system: review covering lakes, coral reefs, grasslands, forests, marine fisheries
studies.outcome_definition: ecological transitions (review)
studies.key_finding: Recent review of 15 indicators (classical CSD, distributional, spectral/complexity) that explicitly names conditional sampling bias: 'Many early warning studies analyze historical time series selected specifically because they ended in a known transition, introducing conditional sampling bias that can spuriously elevate indicator trends'; suggests comparing variance trends against independent proxies of external forcing variability when experiments are infeasible.
studies.notes: Published 2 June 2026; author list not visible in snippets. Most recent review found; useful for stating that outcome-conditioning is an acknowledged, still-open problem.

studies.citation: Jäger G & Füllsack M (2019) Systematically false positives in early warning signal analysis. PLoS ONE 14(2):e0211072
studies.baseline_comparator: null system classes with no critical transition that nonetheless show EWS
studies.data_system: theoretical system classes plus application to real-world data (dataset not visible in search results)
studies.outcome_definition: critical transition; identifies classes of systems without one
studies.key_finding: Identifies 'whole classes of systems that always show early warning signals, even though they do not feature critical transitions', discusses strategies to avoid such systematic false positives, and tests the insights on real-world data.
studies.notes: Supports including a false-alarm budget and evaluating on non-transitioning series.

studies.citation: van der Bolt B, van Nes EH & Scheffer M (2021) No warning for slow transitions. Journal of The Royal Society Interface 18(176):20200935
studies.data_system: models/simulations of slowly responding systems
studies.outcome_definition: tipping point in slowly responding systems
studies.key_finding: Dynamical indicators of resilience require 'observational records ... long enough to capture the response rate of the system', and drivers must change slowly compared to the response rate; when forcing is fast relative to slow-responding systems, estimating resilience from modern time series is difficult.
studies.notes: Gives a principled reason why series length relative to generation time/response rate should be an eligibility criterion or covariate.

studies.citation: Burthe SJ et al. (2016) Do early warning indicators consistently predict nonlinear change in long-term ecological data? Journal of Applied Ecology 53:666-676
studies.baseline_comparator: none (classification of series into true/false positives/negatives; no state/trend forecasting baseline visible)
studies.data_system: long-term ecological monitoring time series (specific datasets not visible in search results)
studies.outcome_definition: nonlinear change detected in the time series (method not visible)
studies.key_finding: Time series containing true positives were uncommon (8% for variance; 6% for autocorrelation), with all but one time series also containing false classifications; 43% of series were categorized differently by variance vs autocorrelation; concludes variance and autocorrelation 'consistently fail to predict nonlinear change' and recommends multivariate, driver-informed approaches.
studies.notes: One of the few empirical evaluations that reports both true and false classifications across many series; a natural precedent for the benchmark's false-alarm accounting.

studies.citation: Gsell AS et al. (2016) Evaluating early-warning indicators of critical transitions in natural aquatic ecosystems. PNAS 113(50):E8089-E8095
studies.data_system: long-term datasets of five freshwater (lake) ecosystems with sudden, persistent transitions of known mechanism
studies.outcome_definition: sudden, persistent regime shift with well-understood ecological mechanisms and drivers
studies.key_finding: Assessed four commonly used EWIs on long-term data from five freshwater ecosystems that experienced sudden persistent transitions; systems were chosen because they transitioned (outcome-conditioned design). Quantitative results not visible in search results.
studies.notes: Relevant precedent for the lake challenge analysis; author list beyond Gsell not visible.

studies.citation: O'Brien DA, Deb S, Gal G, Thackeray SJ, Dutta PS, Matsuzaki SS et al. (2023) Early warning signals have limited applicability to empirical lake data. Nature Communications 14:7942
studies.baseline_comparator: not visible in search results (classic vs second-generation EWS methods compared)
studies.data_system: multi-trophic planktonic time series from multiple lakes worldwide
studies.outcome_definition: classified lake dynamics into forms of abrupt change; critical transitions vs other abrupt change
studies.key_finding: Found few instances of true critical transitions, with different trophic levels often expressing different forms of abrupt change; classic and second-generation EWS 'have been poor in their prediction of change', raising doubts about practical utility; urges considering mechanisms and not using EWS alone as evidence of approaching tipping points.
studies.notes: Most directly comparable recent multi-system empirical evaluation; classifies series by dynamics before evaluation, which parallels the benchmark's outcome definition step.

studies.citation: Litzow MA & Hunsicker ME (2016) Early warning signals, nonlinearity, and signs of hysteresis in real ecosystems. Ecosphere 7(12):e01614
studies.baseline_comparator: none; compares EWS support between studies with demonstrated nonlinearity vs linear/undetermined dynamics
studies.data_system: meta-analysis of published EWS studies plus eight northeast Pacific Ocean time series
studies.outcome_definition: nonlinear ecological transitions/hysteresis (tested via nonlinearity tests)
studies.key_finding: Published studies demonstrating nonlinearity in ecosystem dynamics are more likely to support EWS predictions than studies with linear or undetermined dynamics; recommends testing for nonlinearity before applying EWS.
studies.notes: Marine (NE Pacific) case; motivates grouping/stratifying by system dynamics class.

studies.citation: Ditlevsen PD & Johnsen SJ (2010) Tipping points: Early warning and wishful thinking. Geophysical Research Letters 37:L19703
studies.data_system: high-resolution Greenland ice-core record (Dansgaard-Oeschger events)
studies.outcome_definition: Dansgaard-Oeschger rapid climate transitions
studies.key_finding: Analysis of a high-resolution ice core excludes the bifurcation scenario for D-O events, 'which strongly suggests that these events are noise induced and thus have very limited predictability'.
studies.notes: Climate-domain precedent for the N-tipping/no-warning argument.

studies.citation: Wagner TJW & Eisenman I (2015) False alarms: How early warning signals falsely predict abrupt sea ice loss. Geophysical Research Letters 42:10333-10341
studies.baseline_comparator: idealized climate model with no bifurcation (a null with no tipping point)
studies.data_system: idealized sea-ice climate model simulations
studies.outcome_definition: abrupt sea ice loss (absent by construction in the model)
studies.key_finding: In an idealized model with no bifurcation and no increased rate of retreat, autocorrelation of summer sea ice area increased under global warming while variance decreased, showing AR1 and variance 'can raise false alarms in the climate system, warning of tipping points that are not actually there'.
studies.notes: A clean demonstration that a trending forcing alone can generate EWS-positive statistics without any collapse; supports comparing against trend baselines.

studies.citation: Dablander F, Heesterbeek H, Borsboom D & Drake JM (2022) Overlapping timescales obscure early warning signals of the second COVID-19 wave. Proceedings of the Royal Society B 289(1968):20211809
studies.data_system: European country-level COVID-19 case data (epidemiological, not ecological)
studies.outcome_definition: onset of second COVID-19 wave
studies.key_finding: CSD-based indicators generally decreased rather than increased before the second wave, explained by transient dynamics and multiple relaxation timescales in a non-stationary epidemic (persistent transient from the first wave prevented timescale separation).
studies.notes: Illustrates the transient/non-stationarity failure mode that also applies to post-perturbation ecological populations.

studies.citation: O'Brien DA & Clements CF (2021) Early warning signal reliability varies with COVID-19 waves. Biology Letters 17(12):20210487
studies.data_system: daily COVID-19 case data across 24 countries
studies.outcome_definition: emergence of a COVID-19 wave
studies.key_finding: Using 'a novel, sequential analysis' of daily case data, EWS reliability depended on the time between successive waves and the mathematical likelihood of a critical transition, with highest accuracy for waves preceded by a long period of suppressed R.
studies.notes: Sequential (time-indexed) application of EWS is visible in the snippet; details of the origin scheme not visible.

studies.citation: Jarvis-Cross M, Kirk D, Krichel L, Luijckx P, Molnár PK & Krkošek M (2025) Early warning signals do not predict a warming-induced experimental epidemic. PLOS Global Public Health
studies.baseline_comparator: experimental control populations held at sub-epidemic temperature (non-transitioning controls)
studies.data_system: laboratory Daphnia magna-Ordospora colligata experimental populations plus simulations
studies.outcome_definition: epidemic emergence induced by warming treatment
studies.key_finding: EWS of epidemic emergence were 'nearly as likely to be detected in populations maintained at a sub-epidemic temperature as ... in populations subjected to a warming treatment that induced epidemic spread'; false positives may limit reliability and utility of EWS.
studies.notes: Controlled experiment with true negatives; a strong recent precedent for false-alarm quantification.

studies.citation: Ben-Yami M, Morr A, Bathiany S & Boers N (2024) Uncertainties too large to predict tipping times of major Earth system components from historical data. Science Advances 10:eadl4841
studies.baseline_comparator: none; uncertainty propagation on CSD-based tipping-time extrapolation
studies.data_system: historical observational/reanalysis time series for AMOC, ice sheets, tropical rainforests (climate)
studies.outcome_definition: tipping time of Earth system components
studies.key_finding: Three uncertainty sources (modeling assumptions for extrapolating historical CSD trends, representativeness of the chosen time series, and uncertainties/preprocessing of observational data) make tipping-time predictions from historical data unreliable, e.g., prior AMOC collapse windows (2025-2095) are not robust.
studies.notes: Climate domain, but the preprocessing/observation-uncertainty critique applies to abundance indices.

studies.citation: Rietkerk M, Skiba V, Weinans E, Hébert R & Laepple T (2025) Ambiguity of early warning signals for climate tipping points. Nature Climate Change 15(5):479-488
studies.data_system: perspective with illustrative analyses (climate); code archived on Zenodo
studies.outcome_definition: climate tipping point
studies.key_finding: Discusses limitations of commonly used EWS and common pitfalls in their application, showing alternative explanations can produce resilience loss 'in the absence of tipping points'; argues for testing the existence of tipping points beyond EWS and proposes a method to quantify the probability of approaching a tipping point.
studies.notes: Marked core because it enumerates pitfalls and proposes probabilistic (calibration-like) framing; climate-focused.

studies.citation: Diekert F, Heyen D, Nesje F & Shayegh S (2025) Do early warning signals of tipping points lead to better decisions? Journal of The Royal Society Interface 22(225):20240864
studies.baseline_comparator: decision-theoretic model with vs without an EWS system
studies.data_system: theoretical decision model (no empirical data)
studies.outcome_definition: crossing a tipping point in a decision model
studies.key_finding: EWS can improve beliefs about a tipping point's location, but 'may also result in more risky behavior in the case that no EWS is received'; also notes current detection methods 'are prone to false alarms' and slowdown 'may be an artifact of nonstationary noise'.
studies.notes: Decision-value framing; useful for motivating why the false-alarm burden must be fixed when comparing alarms.

studies.citation: Authors not visible in search results (Beijing Normal University, TU Munich, PIK) (2025 preprint; Science Advances 2026) The influence of data gaps and outliers on resilience indicators / Data gaps and outliers distort critical-slowing-down-based resilience indicators
studies.baseline_comparator: none; mathematical analysis plus synthetic and empirical data
studies.data_system: synthetic time series and empirical Earth-system data (specific datasets not visible)
studies.outcome_definition: not applicable (indicator behaviour, not transition outcomes)
studies.key_finding: Mathematical analysis shows the agreement between variance- and AR1-based indicators is 'fundamentally driven by the time series' initial data point'; missing values substantially weaken indicator agreement, and outliers introduce systematic biases leading to overestimation of resilience.
studies.notes: Directly relevant to gappy, outlier-prone monitoring series (survey indices, GPDD, LPD); author names not visible in snippets.

studies.citation: Arumugam R, Guichard F & Lutscher F (2024) Early warning indicators capture catastrophic transitions driven by explicit rates of environmental change. Ecology 105(4):e4240
studies.data_system: ecological models with explicit rates of environmental change
studies.outcome_definition: catastrophic transition under explicit rate of environmental change
studies.key_finding: With an explicit rate of environmental change, catastrophic transitions 'can become distinct phenomena from bifurcations, and result from a delayed response to noncatastrophic bifurcations', altering what EWS should be expected to capture.
studies.notes: Rate-dependent tipping perspective complementary to the 2025 Sci Rep paper.

studies.citation: Authors not visible in search results (2021) When and Where We Can Expect to See Early Warning Signals in Multispecies Systems Approaching Tipping Points: Insights from Theory. The American Naturalist 198(1)
studies.data_system: theory/multispecies models
studies.outcome_definition: tipping point in multispecies systems
studies.key_finding: Theoretical treatment of which species/variables in multispecies systems are expected to show EWS; details not visible in search results.
studies.notes: Only title, venue and DOI visible; relevant to choosing which population index to monitor.

studies.citation: Authors not visible in search results (2018) How one might miss early warning signals of critical transitions in time series data: A systematic study of two major currency pairs. PLOS ONE
studies.data_system: financial (currency pair) time series
studies.outcome_definition: not visible in search results
studies.key_finding: Title indicates a systematic study of how methodological choices can cause EWS to be missed; content not visible in search results.
studies.notes: Only title visible; included for breadth on window/parameter sensitivity outside ecology.

studies.citation: Authors not visible in search results (2024) Slow down and be critical before using early warning signals in psychopathology. Nature Reviews Psychology
studies.data_system: perspective (psychopathology)
studies.outcome_definition: not visible in search results
studies.key_finding: Cautionary perspective on applying EWS in psychopathology; content not visible in search results.
studies.notes: Only title and venue visible; cross-domain evidence that methodological caution about EWS is widespread.

studies.citation: Cerini F, Childs DZ & Clements CF (2023) A predictive timeline of wildlife population collapse. Nature Ecology & Evolution
studies.data_system: not visible in search results
studies.outcome_definition: wildlife population collapse
studies.key_finding: Proposes a timeline of signals preceding wildlife population collapse; content not visible in search results.
studies.notes: Author list inferred only from the title appearing alongside Clements/Ozgul results; treat authorship as not confirmed by snippet text. Included because it is a recent population-collapse EWS synthesis.
